items.title: The node's Karma payments (#450)

milestone.title: Phase 6 - Karma
milestone.description: Implement Karma/Kizmet and use it throughout

items.body:
- Closes #450 


Phase 6 Step 132. The node queues its own payments, each 0.01% of its balance at the head, rounded down, and none under 10,000 Kismet, in karma/payments.json, and puts them up together as one transaction once karma.payment_batch (100) are queued, or karma.payment_interval_seconds (3600) have passed since its last transaction (KarmaLedger 4.6). The transaction pays each recipient its payments summed, no fee, is created in the head's generation, and is kept in the file, unmined, until it is put up, so that a node that stops mines it again with the same created and never pays twice. It is mined for karma.transaction_seconds (10), signed by the node, and given to Step 131's TransactionsPutUp.

- karma/payments.py: Payment, PaymentQueue, NodePayments (pay, put_up).
- TransactionsPutUp.take returns whether it is done with a transaction, so that one whose key is asked for, or that cannot be carried, is given again.
- KarmaConfig.payment_batch, payment_interval_seconds, transaction_seconds; the module puts up the payments due as it looks. Nothing queues a payment yet: Step 133 will.
- Docs: Phase 6.md write-up and calls, File Layout, Module System, Operator Guide, example configuration; Step 131's checkmark.

I've implemented issue #450 (Phase 6 Step 132, the node's payments) as one commit, 70853ea. It's pushed to a new remote branch, `users/marcp/issue/450/node-karma-payment`. All checks pass: 6,560 tests passed (2 skipped), black, flake8, mypy and pylint are clean, coverage is 98.46%, and `--check-config` passes.

**What it does**
- **Queuing:** each payment is 0.01% of the node's balance at the head, rounded down. Nothing is queued while the node holds under 10,000 Kismet or follows no chain. The queue is kept in `karma/payments.json` (new code in [payments.py](src/libranet/karma/payments.py)).
- **Batching:** the queue becomes one transaction once `karma.payment_batch` (100) payments are queued, or `karma.payment_interval_seconds` (3600) have passed since the node's last transaction. It pays each recipient their payments added together, with no fee, and its `generation` is the head's.
- **Never paying twice:** the transaction is saved in the file, unmined, until it is put up. After a restart it is mined again with the same `created`, so it is still the same payment. It is mined for `karma.transaction_seconds` (10), signed by the node, and handed to Step 131's put-up code.
- **Change to Step 131:** [putting.py](src/libranet/karma/putting.py)'s `take` now returns whether it is finished with a transaction. It returns false only when the sender's key is still being fetched or `carried.json` can't be written, and then the payment is given again at the next look.
- **Nothing queues a payment yet.** Step 133 will call `NodePayments.pay` once nodes are rated.

The docs are updated in the same commit: the Phase 6 write-up (with Step 131's ✅), File Layout, Module System, Operator Guide and the example config.

**Size:** 499 added lines of non-test Python, against an estimate of 300, plus 646 lines of tests. A first version came to 505, just over your 500 limit, so I tightened `payments.py` rather than split the step.

**Decisions for you to review** (also listed under Step 132 in `Phase 6.md`):
1. A node that has never made a transaction puts up its first payments at its next look, since there is no last transaction to count the hour from.
2. If a transaction can't be handed over (key missing, or `carried.json` can't be written), it is re-mined every look rather than stored already mined. That is 10 seconds of mining each minute until the problem clears.
3. If a transaction would be made in the same second as the node's last, its `created` is set one second later, so the two never share a key.
4. If the blocks needed to read the node's balance aren't held, the payment is dropped and logged rather than held until they arrive.

There is also a side effect of Step 131's decision to remember what it has put up only in memory. If the node restarts after a transaction is taken but before `payments.json` is cleared, it is put up once more at the same head. It keeps the same key, so the chain still takes only one, and a test now checks this.

On GitHub, you'll need to open the PR from this branch for #450. Step 132's ✅ goes in once it's merged.

items.title: Make the six venture answers consistent, sourced and honest
items.body:
## Why
The answers to the six venture questions (who uses it, current alternatives, how many, why better, will they pay, unsolved problem) lived in **four places that contradicted each other**:

| Item | Copies disagreed |
|---|---|
| Market size | 24.8 crore in one copy, 26 crore in another |
| NIOS learners | 3.5 lakh vs 27 lakh |
| Pricing | Three different price ladders |

Several answers also claimed AI capabilities the code does not have, and some "official" sources pointed at non-official domains.

## What changed
- **Canonical answers** in `docs/00-venture-strategy-and-naming.md` Section 2:
  - Who: CBSE Class 6-8 parents as the starting segment.
  - How many: built up from the bottom, about 20 lakh families.
  - Why better: answered honestly as "designed, not built".
  - Will they pay: pilot pricing at INR 199 or 499 per month.
  - Unsolved problem: "diagnosis plus follow-through".
- **`/justification`** rewritten to match. It now opens with a Reality Check table that labels each capability Built, Designed or Hypothesis.
- **Venture tab** now renders the bilingual `VentureThesisView` (English and Hindi). That component was previously unused dead code; it replaces a stale inline table, and its missing styles are fixed.
- **Verified figures:**
  - UDISE+ 2024-25: 24.69 crore students, 14.71 lakh schools.
  - NSS CMS: Education 2025 (PIB, 26 Aug 2025): 27.0% of students take private coaching (30.7% urban); average urban coaching spend is INR 3,988 per student per year.
  - CBSE Class 10 registrations 2025: about 23.85 lakh. This one is secondary-reported and labelled as such.
- **Official sources:**

  | Old link (not official) | New link |
  |---|---|
  | `cisceboard.org`, `ciseresults.org` | `cisce.org` |
  | `dpdpa.com` | MeitY Gazette PDF of the DPDP Act |
  | `righttoeducation.in` | `education.gov.in/rte` |

  Also added `SRC-MOSPI-CMSE-2025` to the source catalog.
- **Demo-data labels:**
  - The self-evolving engine events are labelled as illustrative.
  - The peer leaderboard is labelled as fictional.
  - The parent-view consent copy, the L1 success message and the workspace subtitle no longer overclaim.
- **Phone layout:** wide tables stack into labelled cards below 640px.
- **Guardrails:**
  - New `scripts/check-venture-thesis-consistency.mjs`, wired into `pnpm test`. It requires the same figures in all three places and bans the retired figures and links. Negative-tested: it fails on `INR 499-1,499` and on a changed price.
  - `verify-responsive-viewports.mjs` now finds the installed Chromium. It previously printed PASS without launching a browser; it now reports SKIPPED when no browser exists.

## Test evidence
- `pnpm test`: all pass.
  - Phase 1: 13/13. Phase 3: 8/8.
  - Em-dash and file-name checks: pass.
  - Thesis consistency check: 7 figures matched across 3 files; 108 files free of retired figures and links.
  - Real Chromium viewport checks at 390, 820 and 1440px on `/` and `/justification`: 0 console errors, 0 overflow.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean. `pnpm build`: success.
- Interactive Playwright run against `next start` at all three sizes:
  - Venture tab works in English and Hindi, including Q5 pricing.
  - Demo labels are visible.
  - 0 console errors.
- Independent review pass done; its findings are fixed in the second commit.

## Not in this PR (found, needs a product decision)
- **"IQ" scoring of children** still runs through `CognitiveDiagnostic`, `DayLevelCalendarTimetable`, `DailyLessonLoop` and `HeaderNav`. For example, the diagnostic turns 5 answers into a "Cognitive IQ" of 95 to 130. Recommend replacing it with per-skill mastery language.
- **Two failures that already existed before this PR** and are not part of `pnpm test`: `scripts/validate-curriculum-data.mjs` reports 63 errors, and `tests/phase1-data-and-schemas.test.mjs` has 1 failing test. Both fail identically on `main`.

items.title: LIHEAP wave 1d: encode Missouri LIHEAP Energy Assistance regular heating assistance

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

items.body:
## Objective

Ship Missouri LIHEAP Energy Assistance regular heating assistance in Axiom as part of LIHEAP wave 1d, covering the scope and effective period of my corresponding PolicyEngine US implementation, with source-grounded RuleSpec modules, a runnable program, and reproducible PE oracle comparisons.

PolicyEngine PR: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10438 (branch `mo-liheap-wave1d`), open, not merged. Head `2b62923ca0` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983`; this issue describes that code. The merged commit will be recorded here when the PR merges.

## Why queued

The signed encoder is blocked for this program for these reasons:

- **No reviewed oracle revision.** Oracle validation needs a reviewed policyengine-us revision. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10438 opened on 2026-10-23 with no reviews yet, so there is no revision to pin.
- **Sources missing from the corpus.** No axiom-corpus manifest on `main` holds 13 CSR 40-19.020, the LIHEAP rule (definitions, eligibility, the medical deduction, the 8% renter payment, the 2017 table); Appendix K FFY26 (the FFY2026 limits and fuel amounts); application MO 886-4576 (8-2026), the only FFY2027 source with printed values; the draft FFY2027 plan; the FFY2024 and FFY2025 plans; RSMo 660.115; 42 U.S.C. 8624; and the FY2026 SMI table (LIHEAP IM 2025-02 Attachment 4). These need ingest. Captured: the October 2025 LIHEAP Policy and Procedure Manual, the edition the branch now cites (`us-mo-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml`), the FFY2026 plan, the 2025 and 2026 poverty guidelines and the FY2027 SMI table.
- **Signed release not checked.** Presence on corpus `main` was checked on 2026-10-23; presence in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us was not.
- **Billed runs.** Each billed encoder run needs separate approval; none has been approved for this issue.

## PolicyEngine implementation

- **PR:** PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10438, branch `mo-liheap-wave1d`, head `2b62923ca0` (2026-10-23), which merges policyengine-us `main` at `6a92d6a983` and closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10428. The branch includes the 2026-10-22 review fixes (among them the source-conflict candidate for rule (14) and a wider disability list for the medical deduction) and the 2026-10-23 switch to the October 2025 manual (user decision): every manual citation now points to that edition; members left out of the household size as non-citizens have their income counted and the child support they pay deducted; earned income and `disability_benefits` of members under 18 are excluded (new list `income/adult_unearned_sources.yaml`; `income/earned_income_min_age.yaml` renamed `income/adult_age.yaml`), while their Social Security and SSI count; the earlier exclusion of members 18 or older in secondary school is gone. A comment the same day records why IRA and 401(k) withdrawals stay excluded. Everything below describes that tree; oracle fixtures will pin the merged commit.
- **Scope:** Missouri LIHEAP Energy Assistance (EA), the once-a-year regular heating payment of the Department of Social Services, Family Support Division, for FFY2026 and FFY2027: Missouri residence; household size counting citizens and qualified noncitizens; countable income of every member, including members left out of the size (earned income of members 18 or older less 20%, unearned income, Social Security net of the Part B premium, Missouri TANF, less child support paid and the $100 monthly medical deduction); the 60% state median income (SMI) limit with the federal 110% poverty floor; the $3,000 resource limit; heating cost through the household's own fuel bill or unsubsidized rent that includes heat; the subsidized-housing bar; the coal denial; the payment by heating fuel; and the renter payment of 8% of annual rent, capped at the fuel amount. Out of scope: the Energy Crisis Intervention Program (ECIP, winter and summer crisis, including equipment repair or purchase), emergency services, supplemental EA payments, cooling and weatherization.
- **Policy periods:** two verified seasons. FFY2026 heating assistance runs October 1, 2025 to May 31, 2026 (plan item 1.1, page 4); FFY2027 runs October 1, 2026 to May 31, 2027 (draft FFY2027 plan, page 4; application, page 1). Missouri variables are annual and read 1 January values: period `2026` is FFY2026 (Missouri SMI $109,229 from `2025-10-01`; the 2025 HHS guidelines through `fpg_year_lag` 1) and period `2027` is FFY2027 (SMI $113,137 from `2026-10-01`; the 2026 guidelines). State parameters carry `2017-05-30` for rule values, `2023-10-01` for values unchanged since the FFY2024 manual (fuel amounts, 60% SMI rate, 20% deduction, adult age, income lists) and `2025-10-01` for the guideline lag and the adult-only list. `programs.yaml` records `verified_years: "2026-2027"`. FFY2027 rests on the 8-2026 application (limits for sizes 1 to 10, unchanged amounts); the DSS copy of the FFY2027 plan reads “Saved -- with Errors”, and the Clearinghouse has no FFY2027 plan or matrix. Above ten members the model keeps 60% SMI rather than the application's $170-per-member addition (user decision 2026-10-21; interpretation 4). Earlier periods are unverified estimates by backfilling: period `2025` reads SMI $105,825 and reproduces the October 2025 manual's Appendix K ($2,751 for one person). Periods after 2027 use the uprated SMI and lagged guidelines: carried-forward estimates.
- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/mo/dss/liheap/`: `mo_liheap`, `mo_liheap_household_size`; `eligibility/` `mo_liheap_eligible`, `mo_liheap_income_limit`; `income/` `mo_liheap_countable_income_person` (person level), `mo_liheap_countable_income`, `mo_liheap_medical_deduction`. No new input variable. The limit reuses `liheap_smi_limit` (`gov.hhs.smi`) and the floor reuses `fpg` and `gov.hhs.liheap.fpg_floor` (1.1).
- **Parameters:** 13 files under `gov.states.mo.dss.liheap`: `amount` (by `heating_type`), `rent_share` (0.08); `eligibility/` `smi_rate` (0.6), `fpg_year_lag` (1), `resource_limit` (3,000); `income/` `earned_sources` (5 sources), `unearned_sources` (14), `adult_unearned_sources` (`disability_benefits`), `earned_income_deduction_rate` (0.2), `adult_age` (18), `medical_deduction` ($100 a month), `elderly_age` (65), `disability_benefit_sources` (8). Plus a `programs.yaml` entry, a changelog fragment and two `source_conflicts/candidates.yaml` entries (interpretations 1 and 3).
- **Tests:** 52 YAML cases in 8 files under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/mo/dss/liheap/` (`mo_liheap.yaml` 6, `mo_liheap_household_size.yaml` 4, `integration.yaml` 3, `eligibility/mo_liheap_eligible.yaml` 13, `eligibility/mo_liheap_income_limit.yaml` 2, `income/mo_liheap_countable_income.yaml` 5, `income/mo_liheap_countable_income_person.yaml` 10, `income/mo_liheap_medical_deduction.yaml` 9). Every case sends `heating_type`. The 2026-10-23 change rewrote person-income Cases 3 and 8, countable-income Case 5 (now $46,320) and integration Case 3 (now $45,760), and added person-income Case 10. All 52 cases passed locally on 2026-10-23 (`policyengine-core test` on the program folder, before merging `main`).

## Module paths and corpus citations

Presence on axiom-corpus `main` (`dce8e44665`, 2026-10-23) was checked on 2026-10-23 against the full manifest list and the Missouri, poverty-guideline and LIHEAP manifests; the signed release was not checked. rulespec-us `main` (`115bad3183`, 2026-10-23) has `us-mo/policies/` (`cms` CHIP and Medicaid eligibility levels, `dss/snap` manual 1105, `income_tax`) and `us-mo/manual/dss/snap`, but no LIHEAP module, no `us-mo/regulations/` or `us-mo/statutes/`, and no `us/` poverty-guideline or SMI module; `us/statutes/42/` holds other sections. ## Interpretations and gaps

1. **Rule payment table against current agency values (source conflict; user decision 2026-10-22).** Rule (6)(D) ties eligibility to the ranges of section (14), 0 to 135% of the poverty level, and (14) prints payments that fall by range. The FFY2026 plan, Appendix K, the October 2025 manual, the draft FFY2027 plan and the 8-2026 application set 60% of SMI for every size and one amount per fuel. The branch applies the agency values; (14) says payments use “metrics established by the division”. Under the rule table, companion test 1 (124% of the guideline, range E) pays $221 for natural gas, and test 10 (176%) is ineligible. Candidate `us-mo:liheap-rule-income-ranges-and-payments` (unreviewed) records this; the code carries no `# Source conflict` marker until registration.
2. **Renter payment rate and base (source conflict; user decision 2026-10-21).** Rule (13) sets “no more than eight percent”; the manual (page 63), the FFY2024 to FFY2026 plans and the draft FFY2027 plan describe 16%. The branch applies 8% (rule over manual and plan), capped at the household's fuel amount (page 63). Unlike interpretation 1, the rule governs here. RSMo 660.115.2 caps Utilicare state-fund renter payments at the lesser of 8% of rent or $100; EA uses federal funds, and the branch does not apply the $100. The base is `pre_subsidy_rent`, the regular monthly rental charge times 12 (rule (13); page 63); page 82 uses the rent actually paid, the same for the unsubsidized renters the branch makes eligible. The note on the rule-ranges candidate records the rate choice.
3. **Federal 110% floor.** 42 U.S.C. 8624(b)(2)(B) bars excluding a household on income below 110% of the poverty guideline. The 60% SMI limits fall below that floor from size 16 in both years, so the branch admits a household whose income is below 1.1 times the lagged guideline (rounded to cents, strict “less than”). Candidate `us-mo:liheap-110-percent-poverty-floor` (unreviewed) records it; no Missouri source mentions the floor.
4. **FFY2027 limits above ten members (user decision 2026-10-21).** The application adds $170 a month for each member above 10. 60% SMI, divided by 12 and rounded, gives the same $8,316 for 11 members but $1 to $2 a month less for 12 to 15 ($8,485, $8,655, $8,825, $8,994 against $8,486, $8,656, $8,826, $8,996); from 16 the federal floor governs. The branch keeps 60% SMI until an FFY2027 Appendix K is published.
5. **Monthly limits and annual income (inferred rounding; simplification).** The published maximums equal the HHS 60% SMI amount for the size divided by 12 and rounded to the nearest dollar, half up (FFY2027 size 1: 35,298 / 12 = 2,941.50, printed $2,942); this reproduces all 30 rows but is not stated. Missouri counts the income of the month before application (rule (9)(B)5; manual pages 30-31); the branch compares annual countable income with 12 times the monthly maximum.
6. **Household and citizenship (proxies).** The SPM unit stands in for the household buying heat in common. `is_citizen_or_legal_immigrant` stands in for the rule's “citizen of the United States or be a legal permanent resident”; the manual (page 44) also accepts an I-94 marked refugee, parolee or asylum, and the model's list adds deportation withheld, Cuban/Haitian entrant and conditional entrant. COFA citizens, eligible from March 9, 2024 (page 44), have no matching model status. Rule (6)(A) requires all members to be citizens, while (8)(A) and the manual exclude the member; the branch excludes the member from the size. A non-citizen applicant makes the case ineligible, and a refusal to document makes the household ineligible (page 43); the model has no applicant or refusal input. Roomers, boarders, live-in attendants and absent members are not identified.
7. **Members left out as non-citizens (readings; user decision 2026-10-23).** Following the October 2025 manual (pages 42-43), their income counts; the FFY2024 manual (pages 23-24) excluded it. The branch also deducts the child support they pay: page 36 deducts payments “paid by any household member to someone not included in the LIHEAP household”, and page 42 calls these members “ineligible household members”. A reading that treats them as outside the household would deny the deduction (companion test 8(b): $49,920 instead of $46,320). The medical deduction still requires a citizen or qualified-noncitizen applicant or spouse: page 36 is silent on a spouse left out of the household, and a non-citizen applicant makes the case ineligible (page 43); companion test 11's undocumented spouse aged 67 gives no deduction.
8. **Members under 18 (readings; user decision 2026-10-23).** Page 38 excludes earned income and “Unearned income from disability” of members under 18 but counts their “SSA income”. The branch excludes earned income and `disability_benefits` (private short- and long-term disability) under 18, and counts Social Security and SSI at any age, reading SSI as SSA income. A child's SSI is paid on the basis of disability, so reading it as disability income would exclude it. A minor's veterans benefits, workers' compensation and `mo_ssp` count. The FFY2024 manual's exclusion for members 18 or older in high school, GED classes or home school (page 42) is gone, matching plan item 1.9.
9. **Interest, dividends, contributions and withdrawals (plan against manual; user decisions 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-23).** Plan item 1.9 checks “Interest, dividends, or royalties” and leaves cash gifts unchecked; the manual excludes interest and dividends (page 38) and counts contributions (page 33), and the application asks for money received from friends, family or organizations. The branch follows the manual. Capital gains are excluded as lump sums (page 38), although page 32 lists the Form 1040 capital gains line among self-employment documents. IRA and 401(k) withdrawals are not counted: the sources are silent, and IRA and Keogh balances count as resources (rule (2)(N); page 40).
10. **Social Security and Medicare (settled).** Plan item 1.9 checks “Excluding MediCare deduction”, and the manual deducts the SMI (Part B) premium for B and C case members paying it (page 36). The branch counts `social_security` net of the computed `medicare_part_b_premium`, floored at zero per person; a Part B premium paid by a member without Social Security (for example a railroad beneficiary) is not deducted. The October 2025 deduction list no longer names Medicare Part D, which the FFY2024 manual deducted, though page 59 still calls the Category A SMI and Part D figures “these deductions”; the branch deducts no Part D premium.
11. **Medical deduction proxies.** The tax-unit head and spouse who are citizens or qualified noncitizens stand in for the applicant and spouse. Disabled means `is_disabled` or `is_blind` with a positive listed benefit (rule (2)(C); page 48); the general veterans, railroad and Social Security dependent and survivor inputs stand in for the disability forms of those benefits and also catch benefits paid for other reasons. Civil Service Disability and Black Lung have no input; `medicaid`, a per-capita value, is read as receipt. The $100 is monthly by inference from rule (2)(H).
12. **Earned income, TANF, veterans benefits and child support (simplifications).** The 20% deduction comes from the manual, not the rule or plan. Each earned source is floored at zero, with net self-employment, partnership and farm inputs for the Form 1040 lines (“don’t include if a loss”); roomer-boarder income has no input. Missouri TANF counts as computed (`mo_tanf`; plan 1.9 checked). Page 34 heads the documentation list with “Veterans Administration Disability Benefits”, while the plan checks VA benefits and the application lists veterans benefits; the branch counts all `veterans_benefits`. The application deducts court-ordered child support paid outside the household, and rule (9)(B)7 asks for that amount; the manual deducts all child support paid to someone outside the household except lump sums; the branch deducts all `child_support_expense`. Foster care, adoption subsidies, allotments, royalties, installment and insurance payments have no input.
13. **Rent income (source structure).** The October 2025 manual places “Roomer-Boarder / Rent Income:”, including rent from land or buildings, under “Earned Income and Documentation:” (pages 31-32), and treats CRP payments as rental income (page 34), while its 20% deduction names roomer-boarder and self-employment income but not rent (page 36). The branch keeps `rental_income` and `farm_rent_income` unearned, without the 20% deduction; reading rent as earned would cut it by 20%. No companion test uses rent.
14. **Fuels (settled and inferred; user decision 2026-10-21).** `heating_type` is a required input; UNSPECIFIED pays $0 (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9754 tracks the default). PROPANE is paid as tank propane; cylinder propane ($177) is unreachable. SOLAR is paid at the electric amount, by inference from plan item 2.5. OTHER has no printed row: eligible, $0. COAL is denied (code O). NONE has no heating cost. Self-cut wood (rule (7)(G)) is not identified.
15. **Resources (proxy).** `spm_unit_cash_assets` (bank, stock and bond assets) stands in for resources; IRAs, Keoghs, deferred compensation and annuities (rule (2)(N); the manual's page 40 list omits annuities) have no asset input, and the subtraction of tax refunds from resources (page 38) is not modeled.
16. **Heating responsibility and housing (proxies).** `has_heating_expense` stands in for an account in the household's name or a landlord bill. Subsidized means `receives_housing_assistance` or `is_in_public_housing`; with heat in rent it bars the household, with its own fuel bill it does not. The rule (7)(B), (C), (E), (F) and (H) exclusions have no inputs.
17. **Appendix labels (source wording).** The manual's Appendix K (page 129) is still labelled “FFY 24” and prints the FFY2025 limits ($2,751 for one person), and its renter text (page 63) points to Appendix E, now the code sheet. The branch takes FFY2026 limits from Appendix K FFY26 and FFY2027 limits from the application; fuel amounts agree in every source.
18. **Years and dates (simplification).** Annual periods read 1 January values, so period 2026 applies FFY2026 to all of 2026, including October to December 2026 in FFY2027. FFY2027 rests on the 8-2026 application and the unaccepted draft plan. Earlier and later periods are estimates (see Policy periods).
19. **Other gaps.** The one EA per year rule, supplemental EA payments, application windows and priority, Category A (SNAP) income from FAMIS, overpayment recovery, supplier participation and funding availability are not modeled.

## Existing corpus starting points

- [us-mo-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-mo-liheap-state-plan-fy2026.yaml)
- [us-mo-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-mo-liheap-benefit-matrix-manual.yaml) (the October 2025 manual, the edition the branch cites)
- [us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-hhs-poverty-guidelines-2024-2025.yaml) (2025 guidelines, FFY2026 floor; 2024 for the period 2025 estimate)
- [us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/blob/main/manifests/us-liheap-annual-figures-2026.yaml) (2026 guidelines and the FY2027 SMI table)

These manifests are discovery starting points. Verify that the needed documents, attachments, tables, and source provisions are present in the signed release pinned by rulespec-us and match the implementation period. Their presence on corpus main alone does not establish complete coverage or release admission.

## Delivery checklist

- [ ] Reconcile the final PE scope, relevant effective periods, inputs/outputs, source conflicts, and exclusions. Record the authoritative source decision for each material conflict or explicitly limit the release scope.
- [ ] Admit missing official sources with captured artifacts and URL/date/hash provenance. Obtain signed ingest/release admission; keep any toolchain/corpus re-pin in a separate gated PR.
- [ ] Generate the required federal/state modules with the approved encoder, using the canonical `us-mo/` layout, grounded proofs, and paired companion tests. Supply every local input in each test.
- [ ] Cover the FFY2026 limits for sizes 1 to 20 and the FFY2027 limits for sizes 1 to 10 with the inclusive ceiling, the rounding of 60% SMI to the published dollar, the 110% floor at size 16 and its strict edge, the $3,000 resource edge, citizens and qualified noncitizens in size, with the income of members left out counted and their child support paid deducted, the 20% earned income deduction with per-source loss floors, the under-18 exclusion of earned income and disability payments with Social Security and SSI counted at any age, every counted and excluded source, Social Security net of the Part B premium, Missouri TANF, child support paid, the $100 monthly medical deduction with the age 65 edge and each disability benefit, all seven fuel amounts and the treatment of solar, other, coal, no heat and unspecified fuel, the 8% renter payment below and at the fuel cap, subsidized housing with heat in rent or its own bill, and any period before 2026 or after 2027 kept in scope. Set heating type explicitly so oracle fixtures do not depend on a changing default.
- [ ] For eligible modules, use local personal-Codex generation and the existing [reviewed-candidate promotion path](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/blob/main/docs/trusted-signing-supervisor.md#reviewed-candidate-promotion): review exact bytes, obtain commit/base allowlisting and production-signing approval, then validate and add manifests without regeneration. Record hashes and run evidence.
- [ ] Assemble and validate the runnable regular-heating program and indexes. Resolve any applicable composition-signing dependency before declaring it shipped; [axiom-encode#1723](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/issues/1723) remains open.
- [ ] Add axiom-oracles concept/input/output mappings and fixtures against an exact reviewed PE revision, replacing any draft pin with the final merged revision for release validation. Document units, periods, inferred behavior, unsupported cases, and mismatch dispositions against official sources.
- [ ] Link the resulting corpus, RuleSpec, oracle, and successful CI/promotion evidence; publish a precise coverage statement. No encoding, signing, or parity success is claimed by this tracking issue.

The existing promotion route can be tested without the five proposed enrolled-producer/notary PRs. It certifies explicitly admitted reviewed content and current validation, not original generation-runtime provenance.

items.title: Payroll: opening YTD balances per employee for a mid-year switch (#433)
items.body:
Closes #433. A company that switches to SlowBooks mid-year can now tell it what the old system already paid each employee, so the wage bases, the 941, the 940 and the W-2 are right for the rest of the year.

## What it is
An **opening balance per employee per year**, dated the day before the first SlowBooks pay run: gross, federal withholding, Social Security wages and tax (employee and employer), Medicare wages and tax (both), FUTA and SUTA wages and tax, pre-tax and post-tax deductions, garnishments, net; state wages, withholding and other taxes per state; employee and employer amounts per benefit code. Three tables (`payroll_opening_balances`, `_state_balances`, `_benefits`), one migration (`a4330b1c2d3e`, off `d3e4f5a6b7c8`), no journal entry: the old system booked that payroll and the opening balance sheet carries the liabilities.

## Who counts it, and who does not
It is an explicit table and each reader opts in, so nothing that moves money sees it by accident.
- **Counted**: `employee_ytd` (so the wage-base checks and the Additional Medicare threshold start from it, and the employee's YTD and the stub PDF's YTD agree); `BenefitYTD` (rebuilt from the stub snapshots plus the opening's benefit rows, so annual caps see it); the **941** for the quarter `as_of` falls in (its wages, withholding and taxes as the old system figured them) and every later quarter's per-employee wage base; the **940** (its FUTA wages are what the old system already counted toward the $7,000; its payments and FUTA tax are the year's); the **W-2 / W-3** (boxes 1–6, 16, 17; an employee paid only before the switch still gets a W-2; the W-2 dict's keys are unchanged so the Form history Check's hashes are not disturbed).
- **Not counted, on purpose**: the tax liability schedule (those deposits were the old system's), benefit remittance bills, the pay-run list, NACHA, the payroll journal, and the state SUI wage report for the switch quarter (a follow-up if wanted).

## Entering it
- **Employee page**, an Opening YTD block under the YTD table: year, as-of date, the amounts, a states sub-table, a benefits sub-table; Save and Delete. The YTD table gains an "of which opening balance" row.
- **Import for everyone**, from the Payroll page: a dry-run plan (rows, notes, errors) then Apply. Two readers, told apart by the header:
  - the **SlowBooks template** (download link beside the button): one row per employee, named columns, a second row for a second state, `Benefit:<code>` / `Benefit employer:<code>` columns. This is the sure path.
  - a **QuickBooks Desktop Payroll Summary** (employees across, payroll items down, a TOTAL column), best effort: Gross Pay, Federal Withholding, Social Security / Medicare employee and company, Federal Unemployment, state withholding and unemployment, Net Pay are matched by name; everything it cannot place is named in the row's note. The report has no taxable-wage lines, so SS, Medicare, FUTA, SUTA and state **wages** come in as 0 and the note says so; fill those in on the employee page (or use the template) before relying on boxes 3 and 5 or the 940. If the layout cannot be read with confidence (no TOTAL column, no employee names, no Gross Pay / Net Pay line) the plan says so and writes nothing. The reader was written against a hand-made fixture in that layout, not a real export; the first real file will tell us what to adjust.
- **Locked** once a pay run in that year is processed: a change or a delete after that needs a reason, and writes a `CORRECT` audit row on `payroll_opening_balances` with the before, the after and the reason. The employee page asks for the reason inline.

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/test_payroll_opening_ytd.py` (26): create / read / replace / validation; YTD includes it and a later run's SS stops at the wage base; `before=` semantics; 941 by quarter with wage-base seeding; 940 FUTA cap; W-2 boxes and an employee with no stubs; BenefitYTD rebuild and cap; the lock, the reason, the CORRECT row; template import plan / apply / replace / lock; the Payroll Summary fixture; the readers that must not see it are unchanged; the JS blocks exist.
- [x] Full suite locally (non-browser); the payroll, benefits, direct-deposit, pay-run-view and tax-form modules.
- [x] CI (lint, pytest, Windows). No new skips, so the Windows budget is unchanged.

## Follow-ups noted, not in this PR
Per-line deduction YTD on the stub PDF; `_ytd_supplemental` (pre-switch bonuses toward the $1M tier); a per-state W-2 split; the 941's Additional Medicare for the opening is figured from its Medicare wages against $200k.

items.title: feat(tempo): add allowed_chain_ids to the charge client (mppx#888)
items.body:
> **Source:** [wevm/mppx#888](https://github.com/wevm/mppx/pull/888) (merge commit [3c14a65](https://github.com/wevm/mppx/commit/3c14a65a7ea55247f943a6c209ce67a1e8c57239))

## Motivation

mppx#888 lets the Tempo charge client restrict which chains it will pay on with an `allowedChainIds` allowlist, alongside the existing single-chain `expectedChainId` pin. pympp only had the single pin, so a client could not express "mainnet or Moderato, nothing else" or reject every chain.

## Summary

- Adds `allowed_chain_ids` to `tempo()` / `TempoMethod`. `None` (default) allows any chain; an empty sequence rejects every charge.
- The challenge's `methodDetails.chainId`, or the client's pinned chain when the challenge omits one, must be in the allowlist. It runs in the shared charge policy check, so disallowed offers are skipped during challenge selection and rejected before signing.
- When both the `chain_id`/`rpc_url` pin and the allowlist are set, a charge must satisfy both, as in mppx.
- Validates entries as integers at construction.
- Adds parametrized cases to `tests/test_tempo_charge_policy.py`.

## Key design considerations

- mppx uses a single allowlist entry to choose the chain when the challenge omits one. pympp always resolves the signing chain from `chain_id`/`rpc_url`, so here the allowlist only restricts chains and does not select one. With no RPC call yet, challenge selection skips an unknown chain unless the allowlist is empty. Signing always knows the chain and checks it again.
- The CLI, validation and session parts of mppx#888 don't apply: pympp has no CLI or Tempo sessions.

Propagated from https://github.com/wevm/mppx/pull/888 (3c14a65a7ea55247f943a6c209ce67a1e8c57239) by Agricola.

items.title: feat(personal): track loans, repayments and what a new loan costs
items.body:
Personal mode can now track money the user borrowed (a bank, a SACCO, a MoMo loan, family). It shows what is left to pay and when the loan will be done, and checks whether a new loan fits the user's monthly income and spending.

Server side (Flo): yegobox/data-connector#71.

## Adding a loan: two ways
Many people don't remember when they borrowed or how much, but they know what they pay each month and roughly when it ends. So there are two modes:
- **I know the details**: amount borrowed, start date, term or monthly payment, and optionally the interest rate. *"I received this money now"* also records it as money in, under *Loan received*.
- **I know the monthly payment**: the monthly payment and the month it ends, with the rate and "what I still owe today" optional. The balance is estimated from these and labelled *estimated*.

While the user types, a preview line shows the balance, the months left and the payoff month.

## What it shows
- **Home card** and **More → Loans**: total owed, what goes out every month, and the debt-free date.
- **Loan detail**:
  - balance, time left, paid off by, interest still to pay, monthly payment, rate, planned end, repaid so far;
  - every repayment, marked as from SMS or typed in;
  - Record a repayment, Edit, Mark as cleared / Reopen, and Delete.
- **"No repayment recorded this month"** on any open loan where none was recorded this month.
- **What if I borrow…**: amount, term and rate. It shows:
  - the new installment and the total interest;
  - the loans the user already pays;
  - money in, and money out without loans, over the last 30 days (the history a device keeps);
  - what would be left each month, and the share of income going to loans.

  The verdict: up to 30% of income is *Comfortable*, up to 40% is *Tight*, above that *Risky*, and *Not covered* when nothing is left at the end of the month.

## Recording repayments
- **Money-out form**: category *Loan repayment* shows "Which loan is this for?" (already picked when there is only one loan). It records the Cash Out, so the money counts as spending, plus a `personal_loan_payments` doc linked by `transactionId`.
- **SMS review (personal mode)**: the same picker when confirming an SMS as *Loan repayment*. The repayment takes the SMS's own date.

## How it works
- **Ditto-only collections** `personal_loans` and `personal_loan_payments`, keyed by `businessId` and soft-deleted. They are not windowed or evicted (only `transactions` is).
- **`flipper_models/lib/personal_loans/loan_math.dart`** (pure, mirrored in data-connector `personal_loans.rs`):
  - Interest works like a bank loan: a fixed monthly installment on a reducing balance, with interest at rate/12. A rate of 0 is plain subtraction.
  - The balance starts from, in order: a balance the user entered, the amount on its start date, or the present value of the remaining installments up to the end date. Each month adds interest and subtracts the recorded repayments.
  - The outlook simulates the installment forward: months left, payoff date, interest left, or "never ends" when the payment is below the interest.
- `personalMovementWriterProvider` now returns the new transaction id.
- 60 new strings in en/fr/rw/sw. **The rw/sw strings need a native speaker's review.**

## Tests
- `flipper_models/test/loan_math_test.dart` (15):
  - the bank formula: 1M over 12 months at 12% gives 88,848.79 a month and 66,185.50 interest;
  - present value, the installment derived from amount and term or dates;
  - balances (no interest, on schedule, an entered balance wins, the estimate from payment and end date);
  - the outlook and "never ends", the "repayment due" rule, the overview, and the affordability verdicts.
- `flipper_dashboard/test/personal_loans_test.dart` (7):
  - form completeness rules, and loans left out of income and spending;
  - the loans screen totals, the due prompt on the detail screen, a details-mode save;
  - a repayment from the form linked to its loan and transaction;
  - the what-if figures and verdict.
- `personal_finance_test` and `sms_review_section_test` still pass (55 with the above).
- Gates: `format_changed.sh`, `architecture_ratchet.sh` (ProxyService count down by one), and `documented_rules_check.py`.

## Not covered
- Money the user **lent** to others.
- The Books ledger still books *Loan received* as owner capital and *Loan repayment* as an expense. Personal mode doesn't show Books, but a 2200 Bank Loan mapping would be the follow-up.
- Not run on a device: there is no Android SDK on this Mac.

items.title: Wallet: purpose of payment on every send + signed invoices
items.body:
Owner, 23 Oct 2026: "I want to see a purpose-of-payment field in the wallet when I pay… The whole world economy will fit inside that little memo." Also: invoicing in the main wallet.

## Purpose of payment
- Send BSV gets a step 3, **What's it for?**: an optional text box (500 chars, live counter) with chips Gift · Invoice · Wages · Rent · Refund · Dinner · Loan. A chip fills an empty box or goes in front ("Rent · March"). A line under it says "Private: saved on this device with the payment."
- The **confirm sheet** shows a "What it's for" box above the line items (with "· public, written on-chain" when that box is ticked). Nothing on the sheet was removed or loosened.
- Saved per account by txid (`bwallet.purpose.<identityAddress>` in localStorage, capped at 2,000) and shown on **History** rows ("For: …"), in the wide table's Description, in a new CSV `purpose` column, and on the printable statement.
- **To the payee:** BRC-169 handle payments carry it as the memo (existing `sendBsv` `memo`). Plain P2P paymail: `sendBsv` has no way to set the P2P note, so it stays private. Changing that means a toolbox change, so it's left out here.
- **On-chain (public)**: an opt-in tickbox, offered only when every recipient is a plain address and it isn't send-all. It adds one 0-sat `{ data, satoshis: 0 }` request (`OP_0 OP_RETURN <utf8 hex>`) through the existing sendBsv path. No new tx-building code.
- `createAction.description`: left alone. `sendBsv` hard-codes it, and BRC-100 caps it at 5–50 chars.

## Invoices
- Receive › **Request / Invoice** opens a full-screen sheet:
  - Amount with a USD/BSV toggle, What's it for (same chips), optional due date, and **Make invoice**.
  - Payee = your bWalletX paymail. Without a $name it asks you to claim one first.
  - After signing it shows the invoice id + amount, a 240px QR, **Copy link** and **Share**.
- Signed with the identity key under the new protocol `[2, 'bwallet invoice']`. It's added to the reserved-protocol registry and hash set, so no dApp can sign an invoice in the user's name.
- Link: `https://web.bwalletx.com/?invoice=<b64url>` (also `bwalletx://invoice?d=…`). Opening it, scanning it, or tapping **Pay invoice INV-… · $12.50** on a bMail letter goes to the Wallet. The Wallet checks the signature, then checks that the paymail's published **pki key** is the signing key. Only then does it pre-fill payee, amount (in USD or BSV) and purpose.
- A tampered amount, payee or purpose, or a valid signature from another key, is refused with a snackbar and nothing is filled in. Opening a link never pays.
- The Send card and the confirm sheet both say **Paying invoice INV-XXXXXXXX from alice@bwalletx.com**. After it's sent, the payer's wallet remembers the invoice was paid and warns if the same link is opened again.
- **My invoices**: open / paid / cancelled, Mark as paid with a txid, Cancel, Reopen.
  - When the cached History has an incoming payment after the invoice was made, for the exact sats (or within 2% of the dollar amount at that day's rate), it offers "Looks paid by … · Mark as paid".
  - It doesn't mark invoices paid by itself: the payee's wallet can't see the payer's note, so the owner confirms.

## Gating
- Nothing is store-gated. This is P2P BSV between users, the same as the existing Send screen: no exchange, no custody, no third-party funds.
- bMail's "Requests" tab is the low-postage/spam box. `invoiceCents` exists only in the example letters, so there was no real request model to wire. Instead, real letters that contain an invoice link get the Pay button.

## Screens (described, no screenshots committed)
- **Send BSV (phone):** below "2 · How much?" sits a new card, "3 · What's it for?". It has a 2-line text box, a wrapping row of gold-outline chips, the privacy line plus a "0/500" counter, and a tickbox for plain addresses. On an invoice, a gold line "Paying invoice … from …" sits on top. The Send button follows.
- **Confirm Send:** the title, then the gold invoice line, then a tinted "WHAT IT'S FOR" box, then the payee line items as before.
- **Receive Assets:** a full-width gold-outline **Request / Invoice** button under the QR.
- **Invoices sheet:** dark full-screen, max 560px wide. A "New invoice" card, then a QR/link card, then the "My invoices" cards with status colours (gold open, green paid, grey cancelled).
- **History:** a white "For: …" line under the amount/asset lines.

`vite build -c vite.config.web.ts` builds clean. I didn't do a live click-through: it needs a signed-in wallet, and I didn't want to create one in the owner's browser. **Please do the 1920/1440/phone check before deploying.**

## Tests
- New `src/mobile/wallet/purpose/purpose.test.ts` (18 tests), covering:
  - cleaning and chips
  - per-account storage and the History merge
  - the OP_RETURN round trip
  - which recipients can take an on-chain note
  - invoice sign/link/parse/verify
  - rejection of a tampered amount, payee or purpose
  - a foreign signing key, or a payee key that can't be found
  - status changes, payer-side "already paid", payment matching
  - the requestPay pre-fill hand-off
  - finding an invoice link in a letter
- Results: prettier ✓, `tsc --noEmit` ✓, eslint `--max-warnings 0` on the changed files ✓, `bun test src`: 4,660 pass, 0 fail. `golden.test.ts` is untouched.

Touches the send path (`BsvWallet.handleSendBsv`), so this needs the owner's `money-ok` review. Not labelled, not merged.

items.body:
Title: Rules discrepancies in Core Set cards and combat timing (FAQ / Rules Reference citations)

---

Hi, and thank you for open-sourcing this.

I'm Claude, an AI assistant, writing on behalf of my user, who is building a private, personal-use digital version of the game. We built your project, ran the test suite (463 examples pass) and played Passage Through Mirkwood and Escape from Dol Guldur through to the end. The animations and the UI showed us what a digital version of this game should feel like: cards sliding between zones and turning over as they are dealt, the magenta/cyan/amber glow on the cards you can use, the narrated game log, one question at a time. We'll be borrowing a lot of those ideas in our own games. Your engine also helped us find bugs in ours. For example, we ended an attack when A Light in the Dark returned the attacker to the staging area, and you correctly don't (FAQ v1.9, Q&A on A Light in the Dark).

While comparing the two engines card by card (the 200 cards of the Revised Core Set and the Dwarves of Durin and Elves of Lórien starter decks), we found the differences below where your code seems to disagree with the official FAQ v1.9, the Revised Core Rules Reference or the errata. Every item was checked by reading the code at cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6. We have not written failing specs, so please treat these as reports to confirm. Links point to that commit.

## Wrong outcomes

**1. Thalin damages a revealed enemy after its When Revealed, Doomed and Surge**
- [`Hero/Cards/Thalin.hs#L17`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Hero/Cards/Thalin.hs#L17) uses `EnemyRevealedWindow After`. [`Game.hs#L984-L991`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Game.hs#L984-L991) queues the When window, `WhenRevealed`, Doomed and the After window, then appends Surge, so Thalin's damage lands after the When Revealed effect and Doomed, and Surge still resolves when he destroys the enemy.
- FAQ v1.9, errata, Thalin (CORE 6): *"When an enemy card is revealed from the encounter deck, Thalin's ability resolves before any keyword or 'When Revealed' card effects on the encounter card."* The Expecting Mischief Q&A adds that an enemy destroyed this way does not resolve its "when revealed" or keyword effects ("resolves the same way as the effect on Thalin").
- Example: with Thalin committed, Eastern Crows (1 hit point, Surge) is revealed. It should be destroyed with no Surge; here it still surges. Dol Guldur Orcs' When Revealed also resolves before Thalin's damage.

**2. Stand and Fight can put a neutral ally (e.g. Gandalf) into play**
- [`Event/Cards/StandAndFight.hs#L17-L29`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Event/Cards/StandAndFight.hs#L17-L29) → [`Matcher.hs#L198-L210`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Matcher.hs#L198-L210) keeps every affordable ally with no sphere test.
- FAQ v1.9, errata, Stand and Fight (CORE 51): *"Stand and Fight cannot return neutral allies from the discard pile, as neutral cards do not belong to 'any sphere.'"*

**3. Two copies of Caught in a Web on one hero cost 2 resources to ready, not 4**
- [`Treachery/Cards/CaughtInAWeb.hs#L22-L27`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Treachery/Cards/CaughtInAWeb.hs#L22-L27): each copy's response needs the hero exhausted and readies it, so paying the first copy readies the hero and the second copy is never paid.
- FAQ v1.9 Q&A: *"The player must pay for each copy of Caught in a Web before the hero can ready… if a hero has two copies of Caught in a Web attached, the player will have to pay 4 resources from that hero's resource pool in order to ready the card."*

**4. Claimed objectives don't count toward the 2-Restricted limit**
- [`Game.hs#L944-L957`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Game.hs#L944-L957) counts only `entities.attachments`. A claimed Gandalf's Map, Dungeon Torch or Shadow Key is an objective entity ([`Objective/CardDefs.hs#L32-L51`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Objective/CardDefs.hs#L32-L51), all `Restricted`), so a hero can carry all three objectives and still take a Restricted attachment without discarding.
- FAQ v1.9 (1.23) Attachments: *"Any objective card that attaches to another card is treated as an attachment in addition to its other card types."* Rules Reference, Restricted: a character can have at most 2 restricted attachments.

**5. Missing action windows inside an enemy attack**
- [`Game.hs#L456-L466`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Game.hs#L456-L466): after a defender is declared, one window opens, then `ResolveShadow` and `AttackDamage` follow with no window between them and none after damage. An undefended attack ([`Game.hs#L518-L520`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Game.hs#L518-L520)) has no window at all.
- Rules Reference, Appendix I timing chart: *6.4.1 Declare defender → ACTION WINDOW → 6.4.2 Reveal and resolve shadow effect → ACTION WINDOW → 6.4.3 Determine combat damage → ACTION WINDOW.*
- Effect: a defense boost can't be played once the shadow card is revealed, and nothing can be played during an undefended attack.

## Edge cases (mostly multiplayer)

**6. Éowyn can only be used by her owner.** [`Hero/Cards/Eowyn.hs#L17`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Hero/Cards/Eowyn.hs#L17): the ability isn't `anyPlayer`, and the cost discards from `a.owner`'s hand. The card says *"This effect may be triggered by each player once each round,"* each player discarding from their own hand.

**7. An attachment played on another player's character stays under the control of the player who played it.** [`Helpers/Window.hs#L184`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Helpers/Window.hs#L184) uses `attachmentOwner`. FAQ v1.9 (1.38): *"When a player plays an attachment on a character controlled by another player, that character's controller gains control of the attachment."* This affects who may use Unexpected Courage, Steward of Gondor and similar cards.

**8. Other players' Sentinels are offered after the attacked player has declared defenders** (when several defenders are allowed, e.g. Stand Together): [`Game.hs#L494-L510`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Game.hs#L494-L510). Rules Reference, Sentinel: *"A character may declare sentinel defense after the player engaged with the enemy making the attack declares no defenders."*

**9. Despair's shadow lasts the whole phase.** [`Treachery/Cards/Despair.hs#L21`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Treachery/Cards/Despair.hs#L21) uses `phaseModifier`, so a defender readied later in the phase still ignores its defense in the next attack. With several defenders, only the first is affected ([`Game.hs#L489`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Game.hs#L489) passes `Just first`).

**10. Dúnhere's +1 attack lasts the whole phase** ([`Game.hs#L547`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Game.hs#L547), `UntilEndOfPhase`). The card gives it only "when doing so", i.e. for that attack; it matters if he is readied and attacks again.

**11. Thicket of Spears also stops enemies that engage that player later in the phase.** [`Event/Cards/ThicketOfSpears.hs#L19`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Event/Cards/ThicketOfSpears.hs#L19) puts a phase modifier on the player. Rules Reference, Lasting Effects: *"If a lasting effect generated by a player card affects in-play cards (or a specified set of cards), it is only applied to cards that are in play (or that meet the specifications of the set) at the time the lasting effect is established."*

**12. Eleanor: the replacement card is revealed before the cancelled treachery's Surge and Doomed.** [`Hero/Cards/Eleanor.hs#L21-L26`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Hero/Cards/Eleanor.hs#L21-L26) reveals the replacement inside the response, ahead of the cancelled card's queued Doomed and Surge (as far as we can tell from the message order). FAQ v1.9 Q&A: *"Any surge or doomed keywords on the card resolve before the new (replacement) card is revealed."*

**13. Caught in a Web with tied threat: the first tied player in turn order always takes it.** [`CaughtInAWeb.hs#L38`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Treachery/Cards/CaughtInAWeb.hs#L38). FAQ v1.9 (1.03), using this card as its example: *"Tom and Kris are tied for the highest threat level when Caught in a Web is revealed, so the first player determines whether the card affects Tom or Kris."*

**14. Sneak Attack + Beorn at the end of the phase: always returned to hand first.** [`Game.hs#L758-L761`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Game.hs#L758-L761). FAQ v1.9 (1.02) uses exactly this case: *"The first player determines which of the two effects resolves first."*

## Not implemented yet (FYI)
- Dark Knowledge has only its −1 willpower; the response that looks at a shadow card is missing ([`Attachment/Cards/DarkKnowledge.hs`](https://github.com/halogenandtoast/LordOfTheRings/blob/cc36deb7da422e4ce1b0a14a639cfa1001dc82b6/src/LordOfTheRings/Attachment/Cards/DarkKnowledge.hs)).
- Lingering Venom, Ungoliant's Swarm (both campaign-mode encounter cards) and Mendor's Support are empty card files.

## Small build note
In a container with the POSIX locale, the test run stopped with a text-encoding error; `LANG=C.UTF-8` fixed it.

Thanks again! Happy to give more detail on any of these.

items.body: couple of remarks I would like to make about the planning feature - the already spent is wrong. I think this happened after I funded things and then pressed the take all money back once I reset the planning, the spent looks good again. so please fix this bug - when starting over, I would like to see the initial screen instead of empty plan - empty plan: - initial: - when a period finishes, I get the initial screen as if I start over again. that is not what I want. instead, two scenarios: - the user did not plan anything ahead (plan y) and only planned the current period's planning (plan x), which means the plan y is supposed to be empty; in this case we want to copy the subjects from plan x over to plan y. the spending in plan y is mostly set back to zero since those are determined based on the transactions in the current period. the funding that is actually spent in plan x is gone. we remove that visually in plan y. the left over funding (for example you funded 300 but only spent 150) that one will either go back to the pool or stay with the subject. if the subject is a long term cost, then it stays. like goals or yearly recurrings or events, where you only pay a fraction of the actual cost so that you dont get hit with a big bill the day when it actually takes place. in these cases we already knew we wouldnt spent the money we funded so those roll over to the new period's planning. however, fundings in regular expense segment do go back to the pool. the roll overs should look just like how it would look if you fund money to the subject. subjects that are not relevant anymore wont go from plan x to y. like events that are in the past, debts that are fully paid - the user did already plan y upfront; in that case we dont do much. we just leave it as is. the user had the chance to update plan y while the user made changes to plan x, so, we dont go and add new subjects or something. - make future planning smarter, so, lets say we have a loan to pay, we add that as subject, and in the current period we will be paying it off, then we dont need to fund anything in the future for that. instead, we should make it 'disabled' and let the user know that the loan will be fully paid off and we dont have to fund again. but of course just because we have funded money doesnt mean we also actually paid off. because of that we 'disable' it for the future planning, but that should be enabled again in case the user did not pay it off and the new period started. - when there are overspent subjects, I would like to have something like a transaction review, a popup/bottom sheet showing the subjects one by one

items.title: [BUG] ICE runs the shim chain before the receiver permission check
items.body:
## Bug Description

`ImportManager.runImport` and `enqueueImport` call `runImport` in `src/ice/runImport.ts`, which runs `convertChain` before `receiver.receive`.

`core.pages` checks `page-create` and `core.files` checks `asset-upload` inside `receive`. Both checks fail closed. They run only after the shim chain, including any shim `fetch` through the egress policy.

A person who will be refused still pays for the conversion.

## Steps to Reproduce

Call `ImportManager.runImport` for `core.pages` as a person who does not hold `page-create`, with a file a shim can read.

## Expected Behavior

The receiver's permission is asked before shim work. A refusal does no conversion and no fetch.

## Actual Behavior

The shim chain runs. `receive` then returns `refused` and nothing is stored.

## Environment

- __OS__: darwin
- __Other__: ngdpbase v5.27.0, `src/ice/runImport.ts` and `src/managers/ImportManager.ts` (`pagesReceiver`, `filesReceiver`)

## Additional Context

`receiversFor` already asks `mayUse` when listing receivers. The run itself does not.

Found in review of v5.27.0. Relates to [the ICE epic](https://github.com/jwilleke/ngdpbase/issues/1979).

## Error Details

```
const leaves = shim ? await convertChain(shim, file, [], spec, partial) : [{ item: file, chain: [] }];
const outcome = await receiver.receive(item, ctx, ...);
```

items.title: feat(documents): recognise indexOnly document types and delete their entries by values
items.body:
**TL;DR:** Protocol 14 adds document types that exist only as index entries. Dash Evo Tool now recognises them, marks their entries read-only so you are not offered edit, transfer or sale, and lets you delete your own entries by the exact values they were created with. Older networks don't get the option.

## User story
As a **Platform developer**, I want to see and delete my entries of index-only document types, so that I can manage data in protocol 14 contracts without paying for actions the network will always refuse.

## Scenario
### Actual behavior
Index-only entries look like ordinary documents. Replace, transfer, purchase and set-price are offered but always refused by the network after the fee is paid, and delete by ID cannot work because these entries are addressed by their values, not an ID.

### Expected behavior
Index-only entries are labelled read-only. Delete fills in the entry's values, checks them before anything is signed, and warns that a value differing from the original entry makes the network refuse the delete while still charging the fee.

## Detailed discussion
Stacked atop #1015 (`chore/bump-platform-v4.3`); built on Platform v5.1-dev `132ae31`.

- **Detection and gate:** `DocumentTypeV2Getters::index_only()`; the delete is available only where the platform version defines `document_index_only_delete_state_transition` (protocol 14). New `FeatureGate::IndexOnlyDocumentDelete`.
- **Model:** new `src/model/index_only_document.rs` with values extraction, JSON round-trip (`$createdAt` split off) and `validate_index_only_delete`, returning a typed `IndexOnlyDeleteError` with the same checks and order as the SDK.
- **Backend:** new `DocumentTask::DeleteIndexOnlyDocument` builds the transition with the SDK's `DocumentDeleteTransitionBuilder::from_values` and DET's identity signer, through a shared `send_document_delete` helper, so token payment, options and action-fee agreement match the by-ID delete. The platform-wallet `delete_document_by_values_with_signer` wrapper is not used: it cannot carry token payment or fee agreement, needs an `IdentityWallet` that key-imported identities lack, and reports refusals as strings. Replace, transfer, purchase, set-price and by-ID delete refuse index-only types before any fetch or signing.
- **Errors:** `TaskError::IndexOnlyDeleteNotSupported`, `IndexOnlyDocumentReadOnly`, `IndexOnlyDeleteRefused`.
- **UI:** document action screen (read-only notice, "Fetch My Entries", editable values with live validation, warning in the confirmation) and a notice in the documents browser.
- User story DOC-013 added.

### Known limitations
- An entry fetched through a subset index can lack optional values; this cannot be detected from the entry. The editable values and the confirmation warning are the mitigation.
- A type with no index starting with `$ownerId` cannot list your entries, so it has no delete from the UI.
- Creating index-only entries is not covered by this PR.

### Testing
- 24 new tests (model, backend, screen, browser) plus an extended protocol 14 gate test; behaviour tests shown failing on a stub first.
- Clippy `--all-features --lib --tests -- -D warnings` clean; document, index-only and feature-gate library tests pass (83); contract screen kittest passes.
- No rendered kittest for the new flow (no private-key fixture in that suite); no live network writes.

items.body:
## Problem

Drivers in Malaysia want to know before they go whether a route has tolls and roughly how much they will pay. #30 adds a "Toll" badge. This issue adds the fee.

## Data

OSM does not carry reliable toll prices for Malaysia. The `charge` tag on toll booths is rare and often stale. Rates are published per plaza and vehicle class by Lembaga Lebuhraya Malaysia (LLM) and by the concessionaires.

- Open system (fixed fee per plaza, for example most Klang Valley expressways): fee = sum of class 1 rates of the plazas the route passes.
- Closed system (PLUS, ELITE, LEKAS and others: fee by entry and exit pair): needs an entry/exit rate table. v1 may show "Toll: fee varies" for closed-system segments if the table is not available.

## Acceptance criteria

- A bundled, versioned data file of toll plazas: id, name, coordinate, system (open or closed), class 1 rate in RM. Sources and last-checked date are in the file header and in docs.
- The route preview shows an estimated toll total for class 1 cars, for example "Toll ~RM 6.30", next to the #30 badge. If any closed-system segment has no rate, show "Toll: from RM X" or "fee varies". Never a fake exact number.
- Matching is on the device, against route geometry. No extra network calls, and no location sent anywhere.
- Unit tests cover plaza matching along a route (including plazas on the opposite carriageway, which must not match) and the fee sum.
- User-facing strings use `String(localized:)`, and amounts are formatted in MYR.

## Done when

- `make lint` and `make test` pass.
- Screenshot: KLCC to KLIA route preview with a toll estimate.

Depends on #30.

items.body:
A process-log entry for `coordinating-epics`, from a run on a host that vendors this repo as a submodule. Per *Adding an entry*, it comes here as an issue: writing it into the vendored copy would leave the host with a modified submodule. The host repo, CannObserv/broker, is public, so the entry names it.

**Please add** the entry below as `process-log/2026/2026-10-23-broker.md`, and its row to `process-log/2026/index.md`.

**For #404:**
- **Finding 7 is a second sighting of #413** (`replace-section` can't rename a heading). No new issue.
- **Finding 8 is a new tool gap,** not yet filed: `scan.sh` reads every cross-repo ref with the host's token.
- **Promotion candidates** (each now seen in two runs): finding 5 with CannObserv/broker#80's 2026-10-14 finding 123 (a doc at its budget is a shared surface), and finding 6 with #428's finding 1 (foreign ticks).

---

## Session 2026-10-23 — CannObserv/broker#22

A design-doc epic: broker's production units moved from the dev checkout to root-owned releases under `/srv/broker`, built by a new `scripts/deploy.sh`. The way in was an approved design (D1-D11) whose Steps table became seven native sub-issues, CannObserv/broker#105 to CannObserv/broker#111. It closed on 2026-10-23 on its exit criterion, after an empty re-scan. The parent epic, CannObserv/broker#80 (logged 2026-10-14), was burning down the same repo's backlog on the same host at the same time, coordinated from its own thread.

### Shape
- **Way in:** a design doc's Steps table, with one tiebreak set from the parent (a released upstream dependency pre-empts the next child, between children).
- **Children:** 7 planned, 7 closed. Mid-run issues: 13 (CannObserv/broker#112 to CannObserv/broker#124), all out of epic (the parent's backlog, a sibling epic's, or follow-ups filed at the end).
- **Check-ins:** creation, 7 check-ins, plus three between-check-in entries (a cross-repo request filed with approval, a floating child started beside a parent child, and a monitor going ready).
- **Days:** 2026-10-17 to 2026-10-23.
- **Stats:** the node's sourced baseline went from 467/4 (`tests/deploy`) and 837/4 (full suite) to 722/4 and 1261/4, with the same four skips throughout. `ACL LOG` stayed at 4 entries from the first read to the last.

### What was different
- **Every child changed production,** one unit at a time; three children ran a rollback drill. Verification read journals, `_UID`s, state files and the deploy log, not merges.
- **Two coordinators shared one deploy script.** The parent's children deployed through the script this epic was building, from C3 on.
- **The coordinator's pre-flight changed a child's scope twice:** C5's `backup.env` edit, and C7's budget question. Both went to the operator as recommendations in the child's thread, before any build.

### Findings that changed the protocol
1. **Two epics deploying through one script need a written rule, not a lock.** `deploy.sh` held a `flock`, which serializes two deploys but doesn't stop the second from rolling the first back: it accepts any CI-green ancestor of `origin/main`. Both coordinators' briefs carried the same rule: before each deploy, read the live symlink and the deploy journal, and deploy only `origin/main`'s tip. Whoever deploys second ships both. That held with no incident while a floating child and a parent child built and deployed side by side, and through the parent's later deploys. **A drill breaks the rule on purpose,** so the rule needs a named exception: the operator approved "back to `<sha>`" by sha in the child's thread.
2. **For a child that changes a unit and its environment together, brief both directions of the switch.** The scope for C5 (drop root) said to edit a host env file that every installed version of the unit reads. Edited before the deploy, the switch back would restore the old unit against the edited file, and both would fail (exit 4, nothing answering). Edited after, the new unit's forced run couldn't read the old path, and the deploy would switch back. The brief's recommendation: put both values in the unit and leave the host file alone. The implementer found a third reader, the restore runbook, which made the case stronger. The rule: for each host file a changed unit reads, ask what the old unit sees after a switch back, and what the new unit sees during its first forced run.
3. **Read drill journals for what ran, not only whether it passed.** One drill tick reported the new build under the old unit. The cause: a timer that fired in the ~0.25 s between the symlink swap and `daemon-reload`. Harmless for that child, but it mattered for the one where code and unit changed together, so it was carried there, and in the end written down as an accepted limit.
4. **Rehearse undocumented runtime behaviour with the unit file itself, before the merge, uploading nothing.** Whether `LoadCredential=` reads its source before `TemporaryFileSystem=` hides it wasn't in systemd 255's man pages. The brief proposed a `systemd-run -p` rehearsal. The implementer corrected that: properties sent over D-Bus may not expand `%d` the way a parsed unit file does. So the real unit file, rewritten by `sed`, ran as a runtime unit in `/run/systemd/system/`, then a second unit with the previous shape proved the rollback's ownership flip. That settled a question a previous child had left open. The brief rule: name the rehearsal's vehicle, and prefer the shipped artifact over a reconstruction of it.
5. **A doc at its budget is a shared surface (second run).** At the last child's hand-off, the policy file had 8 tokens of headroom, and the recovery runbook was 1.4k tokens over its budget. Each of the two previous children had noted the overage and left it for "the rewrite". The pre-flight measured both exactly from the repo's context metrics, and turned the Verify item "budgets hold" into an operator question before the build. The answer was to move dated history to an archive doc. **Rule:** at each hand-off, read the exact headroom of every doc the child will touch, and when a child defers an overage, name the child that will pay it.
6. **With native sub-issues, GitHub ticked the epic's box when a child closed, whoever closed it.** Seen on C4, C5 and C7 at least. Each tick was verified first, then accepted with `--accept-ticks`. The parent run found auto-ticks unreliable with plain task lists; with sub-issues they were consistent. That was still a claim each time, never evidence.
7. **`replace-section` can't rename a heading.** Retiring the design brief's "Interim" convention needed a new heading. The section kept its old heading, with a "Retired" line leading its new body. Second sighting of #413.
8. **`scan.sh` reads every cross-repo ref with the host repo's token.** One ref in a repo that token can't see returned a 404 warning at every check-in, and the coordinator had to read it by hand with that repo's own token. A per-owner token map, or a `--token-env OWNER=VAR` flag, would close the gap.
9. **Hand a parent epic its changes as a ready-to-write comment.** The last child rewrote the parent's verify recipe, which this coordinator doesn't own. The implementer posted the replacement text, part by part, on the child. The closing report on the parent links it, for the parent's coordinator to write through `epic-edit.sh`. The same was done for this epic's own retired section. Neither coordinator edited the other's body.
10. **An approval given in the operator's session was posted on the issue, quoted and timestamped,** by the implementing thread ("Operator approval, given in the agent session at ..."). Each scope change and each sudo step then had an auditable approval on the child, which the coordinator could cite at verification. Worth adding to the implementer contract.

### What the scripts caught
- `epic-edit.sh`'s lint refused a short cross-repo ref (`status#51`) in a note.
- `--dry-run`'s diff showed that a `note` re-stated a field already on the line (`note` appends), before the write.
- `--scan` refused nothing this run: every new issue was in the log line before the write.

### Index row
| [2026-10-23](2026-10-23-broker.md) | CannObserv/broker#22 | Design-doc epic, 7 children moving production onto releases, beside its parent epic on one host. A tip-only deploy rule across two coordinators; brief both directions of a unit's switch; rehearse with the unit file itself; a doc at budget is a shared surface (2nd run) |

items.body:
Let workers set their own price, and make the server enforce it.

## Problem
The client posts a `budget` and the amount paid into escrow is whatever the client sends. `POST /api/payments/stk-push` and `POST /api/escrow/fund` accept any `amount` and never check it against the job (they don't check the job's owner, assigned worker or price either), so a client can pay less than the work is worth. Workers have the experience to price their own work.

## Scope
**Backend**
- [ ] Applications carry a worker `price` (and the job's `currency`, copied by the server)
- [ ] `POST /api/jobs/:jobId/apply` requires `price`; new `PATCH /api/jobs/:jobId/application` lets a worker edit their quote while it is pending and the job is open
- [ ] Choosing a worker copies the quote onto the job as `agreedPrice` / `agreedCurrency`, which locks it
- [ ] The amount paid is derived from the job on the server (converted to whole KES when the job is not in KES); the client can no longer set it. A mismatching `amount` returns 409
- [ ] `initiateEscrowPayment` and `fundEscrow` check the job exists, belongs to the caller, is assigned, and the worker matches
- [ ] `settlePayment` only funds the escrow when the agreed price still matches the price recorded when the payment started
- [ ] Browse jobs returns the worker's own application (`myApplication`) so the UI survives a reload
- [ ] Jobs created before this change fall back to `budget`
- [ ] Update and add tests (apply, select, stk-push, escrow fund, settle payment), and the backend README

**Frontend**
- [ ] Job card: show the client's budget as a guide and an inline "Send your quote" panel (price, optional message, a note that the price is locked once chosen); "Quote sent: KES X" with Edit quote afterwards
- [ ] Choose a worker: each applicant's quote, a "above/below your budget" chip, sort by lowest price or highest trust, and a confirmation ("You will pay KES X into escrow. The worker is paid only when you approve the work.")
- [ ] Pay screen shows the agreed price, read-only, and sends no amount
- [ ] Relabel the job budget as a guide and show the agreed price on job cards and the wallet page

## Notes
- Part of the pair with the worker KYC issue; this one goes first because it closes the underpayment gap.
- Edits the M-Pesa settlement code from #113, which is merged.
