items.body:
## Problem

Group expenses can be split equally, by exact amounts or by percentages. Sometimes the natural way to split is by "parts": nights each person stayed, people per household, and so on. Today I have to work out each person's amount on a calculator (or turn the parts into percentages) before typing it in.

## Proposed Solution

Add a "Shares" option next to equal, exact and percent, like Splitwise's "Split by shares". You type a number for each person, and each one pays their number divided by the sum of all the numbers.

Example: a 900.00 rental house for a week-long trip. Ana stayed 5 nights, Bruno 3 and Carla 7. I'd just type 5, 3 and 7, and Securo would split it as 300.00, 180.00 and 420.00.

The total is $5 + 3 + 7 = 15$, so:

- Ana: $900 \times \frac{5}{15} = 300.00$
- Bruno: $900 \times \frac{3}{15} = 180.00$
- Carla: $900 \times \frac{7}{15} = 420.00$

What I'd expect:

- One number field per member (starting at 1), showing how much each person will pay as you type.
- The numbers can be anything above zero, and don't have to add up to anything.
- The numbers are saved, so editing the split later shows what was typed (percentages already work this way).
- Available wherever splits can be set today: the transaction dialog, the "add to group" bulk action and agent proposals.
- Rounding works like the other split types: amounts go to the cent and the last person gets any leftover cent, so the total always matches.

## Alternatives Considered

Percentages and exact amounts both work, but the math has to be done outside the app first. Equal split only covers the case where everyone counts the same.

## Additional Context

I looked at the code a bit: the split logic is in `backend/app/services/split_service.py` and the split types are defined in the schemas. My preference is to save the typed numbers. That probably needs a new column on `transaction_splits` plus a migration, and the numbers would show up again when editing the split later.

If that's too much work, a simpler alternative is to do it like Splitwise, which doesn't save the shares at all: the frontend just calculates the amounts and saves them as fixed values (the existing `exact` type). That loses the record of how the split was calculated, so editing it later would show only the amounts, but it's a much smaller change, mostly in `transaction-splits-section.tsx` and the dialogs that use it, with no backend or migration work.

I didn't find an existing issue for this.

items.body:
## Goal

The pitch deck, the pitching video and the sample roadmap answer the feedback from our 23 October mentor session before the repository freezes at 7:59:59 AM MYT on Sunday 25 October 2026. Aim to submit on Saturday 24 October by 11 PM.

This issue holds everything an agent needs: what the mentor said, why it matters, what the team decided, and the work. Refine the details within the decisions. Don't reverse a decision without the team.

Contents:

1.  [Source](#source)
1.  [What the mentor said](#what-the-mentor-said)
1.  [Diagnosis](#diagnosis)
1.  [Decisions](#decisions)
    1.  [Decision 1: one user, one payer, one moment](#decision-1-one-user-one-payer-one-moment)
    1.  [Decision 2: who pays](#decision-2-who-pays)
    1.  [Decision 3: narrate what the user or payer gets](#decision-3-narrate-what-the-user-or-payer-gets)
    1.  [Decision 4: make MCP the stand-out moment](#decision-4-make-mcp-the-stand-out-moment)
    1.  [Decision 5: name the course platforms](#decision-5-name-the-course-platforms)
1.  [Current](#current)
1.  [Desired](#desired)
    1.  [Package A: roadmap cost and funding route](#package-a-roadmap-cost-and-funding-route)
    1.  [Package B: real people](#package-b-real-people)
    1.  [Package C: deck](#package-c-deck)
    1.  [Package D: video](#package-d-video)
    1.  [Package E: judge questions](#package-e-judge-questions)
1.  [Key interfaces](#key-interfaces)
1.  [Acceptance criteria](#acceptance-criteria)
1.  [How to test](#how-to-test)
1.  [Must not change](#must-not-change)
1.  [Out of scope](#out-of-scope)
1.  [Blocked by](#blocked-by)
1.  [Done means](#done-means)
1.  [Sources](#sources)

## Source

- **Session:** 23 October 2026, 4:20 to 4:36 PM MYT, 15 minutes on Zoom, with a venture-capital and business-strategy mentor. The feedback was about business strategy, not the technology.
- **What the mentor saw:** our five-slide mentor deck and the spoken pitch. The live demo didn't happen because the mentor's connection dropped. They judged Kotak from the slides, not from the running app.
- **Full transcript:** local only, at `docs/meetings/2026-10-23-mentor/transcript.md` on the maintainer's machine. `docs/meetings/` is gitignored because the calls name people who didn't agree to publication. Never commit it or paste it into GitHub. An agent on that machine may read it.
- **Declaration trail:** `docs/TECH-DECLARATION.md` points to #98 for this feedback, and #98 points here.

## What the mentor said

Eight points, in plain English, in the order they came:

1.  **Explain the business model.** How will Kotak keep running: investor money, or a business that pays for itself?
2.  **Pick one target user.** "Working adults" means everyone, and many similar products already hold that broad market. Through TalentCorp, the group could be fresh graduates, Malaysians abroad who want to come home, or skilled workers. Through HRD Corp, it is people who already have a job and want to reskill. Each group needs a different approach and different promotion.
3.  **Give more depth after the check-up.** Three minutes looks easy, but what does the user get? Show what each reskilling option costs, which reskilling is popular now, and what suits the user or the company they want to join.
4.  **Make it useful, not flashy.** Don't make the site look "very AI" or fancy. Put yourself in the user's place, and talk to real people in that group.
5.  **Use HRD Corp funding.** HRD Corp funds reskilling with government money. List the courses it sponsors. Kotak itself may qualify for a grant. Without grants, Kotak needs its own business model.
6.  **Know exactly who your client is.** Then it is easier to satisfy them, and to make them, or whoever needs them, willing to pay.
7.  **Win a stranger in five minutes.** A visitor who doesn't know you leaves within five minutes if the site only looks cool and gives nothing useful.
8.  **Use real cases and study competitors.** Put a real case study and real course costs in the demo. Study MasterClass and a Malaysian reskilling platform heard as "ReSkills" (see [decision 5](#decision-5-name-the-course-platforms)). Find how Kotak differs, so people choose it in a specific situation.

We planned three questions: where a judge would dock us first, whether the April-to-May change proves that the trend layer drives matching, and which buyer to test first. The mentor didn't answer them one by one. The feedback still answers two of them: the weak spots are a broad user, a thin output and no business model, and the buyer to test first is one narrow client. The April-to-May question stays open (package E).

## Diagnosis

- **The pitch, not the engine, is the main lever.** The mentor never saw the running app. Their "what do they get?" came from a pitch that spent more time on how Kotak works (fixed rules, architecture, MCP) than on what the user walks away with.
- **Our opening line contradicted our position.** We called Kotak "a three-minute AI check-up". Our position is that data decides and the AI only explains (`docs/PRODUCT.md`).
- **The rubric agrees with the mentor.** Innovation (30%) asks for "a sharply framed slice of the workforce problem (a specific user and moment of need)". Clarity (20%) asks that a cold listener can say who the user is and what they walk away with (`docs/sources/drive.google.com/domain-1-aiversecity.md`, section 8).
- **One product gap no slide can hide.** All 11,040 roadmap resources in `data/generated/role-corners.json` (923 roles) are unverified Google search links (`kind: "search"`, `verified: false`). Real courses exist only in the sample profile in `apps/web/src/demo/data.ts`: GitHub Skills, W3C WAI Easy Checks, MDN's ARIA guide and freeCodeCamp's Quality Assurance course, all free. Judges use the live link themselves (`docs/BRIEF.md`).

Where each point lands:

| Fix in         | Mentor points             | What changes                                                                    |
| -------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Deck and video | 1, 2, 5, 6, 7             | One persona and one moment, a "Who pays" slide, the outcome before the mechanism |
| Product        | 3, and the costs in 8     | A cost on each roadmap step and a funded route, on the sample profile          |
| Real people    | 4, and the real case in 8 | 3 to 5 people from the chosen group try Kotak                                   |

## Decisions

The team made these on 23 October 2026, after the session.

### Decision 1: one user, one payer, one moment

| Part            | Choice                                                                                     | Why                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Who             | Software and digital workers in Malaysia: developers, testers, designers                   | The sample profile, the What Changed flip and the real courses are all built around a front-end developer. Any other job means rebuilding the demo. |
| Where           | At an employer that pays the HRD Corp levy                                                 | The employer is the payer, through the levy it already pays                                                                                          |
| Moment          | The company rolls out AI coding tools, and the manager asks what training to fund this year | A specific week, not a vague worry. Refine the words; keep the shape.                                                                               |
| Walks away with | A dated 12-week plan: free steps first, then training the employer can fund                | Answers "what do they get?"                                                                                                                          |

- **Narrow the pitch, not the engine.** The engine keeps all 923 jobs. That becomes one line of proof: "The same engine covers 923 jobs. We start here."
- **No PRD change.** "Digital workers first" sits inside the PRD's "working adults" (`docs/PRD.md`, section 2.1). Keep the signed PDFs in `submission/` as they are.
- **The judge question to expect:** why not the most vulnerable workers? Answer: AI is changing software work first, and the AI-usage data covers it best. Other jobs follow as the data grows.

### Decision 2: who pays

- **Workers** use Kotak free.
- **Employers** pay for a team view that shows where to spend their HRD Corp levy. Registered employers pay a monthly levy of 1% of wages, or 0.5% in the optional category, and claim approved training from it ([HRD Corp FAQ][hrd-faq]).
- **Agencies** such as TalentCorp and HRD Corp get the anonymous national view, which shows totals only for groups of 10 or more.
- **The team view isn't built.** It is the domain's optional "Employer / HR view" (domain file, section 5). Present it as the next step, never as a working feature.
- **No invented prices.** A number on the slide needs a source. Otherwise, leave numbers out.
- **Grants:** the mentor said Kotak itself may qualify for one. Name it as a route to explore. Don't name a specific grant without a source.

### Decision 3: narrate what the user or payer gets

Name a feature in the pitch only if it answers "what does the worker or the payer get?"

- **Kopi stays, and the narration says what it does.** Kopi explains each verdict in plain words while fixed rules decide. Let Kopi's voice play in the What Changed shot (D6). Keep its lines short and inside the speech bubble, so judges never take it for AI narration, which the video rules ban (`docs/demo/video.md`).
- **Live2D and ElevenLabs stay out of the narration and the product copy.** Name them only on the technical slide, in `docs/TECH-DECLARATION.md` and in the README.
- **The Live2D credit stays on the landing page** (`apps/web/src/views/landing/LandingEvidence.tsx`). Live2D's licence requires that notice, word for word (`docs/DESIGN.md`).
- **Kotak isn't an "AI check-up".** Say "a three-minute check-up for your job" or similar.

### Decision 4: make MCP the stand-out moment

- **Show it.** Record a clip of about 15 seconds: an AI assistant calls Kotak at `/api/mcp` and gets the same verdicts as the web app. Any MCP client works, such as Claude Code.
- **Say it in one line.** "Most teams build a chatbot. Kotak is the tool a chatbot calls." The rubric asks for more than "upload a CV and ask a chatbot for jobs", and the briefing warned that teams lose marks for over-depending on AI (`docs/BRIEF.md`, Judging). Here the assistant reads our fixed rules instead of guessing.
- **Tie it to the payer.** On the "Who pays" slide, add one line: an employer's own HR assistant can use the same tools.
- **Pay for the time.** Cut the phone shot D8 (10 seconds). Slide 7 already shows the phone and desktop layouts.
- **Let judges try it.** Put the app's Connect Your AI page (#192) on the closing slide.

### Decision 5: name the course platforms

Add these to the innovation slide (slide 8), beside MyMahir and LinkedIn:

- **MasterClass:** subscription video courses taught by well-known experts.
- **ReSkills:** a Malaysian subscription platform of live online classes, which says it is an HRD Corp-registered training provider ([NST, 2021][nst]; [Vulcan Post][vulcan]). Most coverage dates from 2021 to 2024, so check its current site before quoting a price or a claim.
- **e-LATiH:** HRD Corp's learning portal, with free and premium courses (`docs/research/prior-art-sdg-courses.md`).

The line: they offer courses; Kotak tells you which skill to learn first and why now, then points you to their courses. They are supply, not rivals.

## Current

- **Deck:** `docs/demo/deck/pitch-deck.html`, 11 slides, exported to `kotak-pitch-deck.pdf` and an image-only `kotak-pitch-deck.pptx` (#215). Slide 1 says "Every Malaysian worker". Slide 3 lists three kinds of worker. Slide 5 names ElevenLabs. Slide 8 compares MyMahir, LinkedIn and two past winners. Slide 10 says Claude Opus 5.5, but the API uses Claude Haiku 5.5 (`apps/api/src/ai/claude.ts`). Slide 11 asks a mentor three questions and is dated 23 October.
- **Video:** the plan is in `docs/demo/video.md`: 5:30 to 6:30, live-demo shots D1 to D8, and D6 What Changed is the key moment. #82 and #84 are open.
- **Roadmap:** each step shows hours a week and a finish date, but no cost and no funding route.
- **Open PRs that change the check-up the video records:** #237, #238, #239 and #259.
- **Related open work with its own owner:** reviewed JobStreet ads per role (#277) and a `job_market` tool for Kopi and MCP (#273). They touch mentor points 3 and 8: what is in demand now, and real Malaysian data. Their owner schedules them. Anything that lands must land before the frontend freeze.

## Desired

Five work packages. Steps that only a person can do are marked **(human)**.

### Package A: roadmap cost and funding route

Frontend, by Friday 23 October, 11 PM.

1.  Show "Free" on each step of the sample profile's roadmap. All four of its courses are free.
2.  Add one HRD Corp card to the roadmap. It states the scheme's rules, not a course list: the employer applies in e-TRiS before training starts, and the training runs at least 4 hours. Link HRD Corp's [claimable courses page][hrd-claimable] and [e-LATiH][elatih].
3.  Never call a specific course "HRD Corp-claimable". There is no public list of claimable programmes (`docs/research/prior-art-sdg-courses.md`).
4.  Check how the app shows the unverified search links. They must read as unchecked search suggestions, never as courses.
5.  Merge or park #237, #238, #239 and #259 by Friday 11 PM **(human)**. Freeze the frontend on Saturday at 12 PM, because the video takes need a frozen build.

### Package B: real people

By Saturday 24 October, 12 PM. **(human)**

1.  Put 3 to 5 people from the chosen group through Kotak, about 15 minutes each.
2.  Note what helped, what was missing, and whether they would start the plan.
3.  Get consent before quoting anyone. Keep quotes anonymous, and commit no personal data.
4.  Describe it honestly in the pitch, for example "5 informal tests", never "a pilot".

### Package C: deck

#80, by Saturday 2 PM. Edit `docs/demo/deck/pitch-deck.html`, then export the PDF and the PPTX again.

1.  Slide 1: the tagline names the chosen group, not "every Malaysian worker".
2.  Slides 2 and 3: one persona and one moment ([decision 1](#decision-1-one-user-one-payer-one-moment)). One sample person, labelled as a sample, replaces the three kinds of worker.
3.  Slide 4: lead with what the person walks away with: the finished roadmap, its hours a week, finish date, cost and funding route.
4.  Slide 5: drop the ElevenLabs name.
5.  A new "Who pays" slide ([decision 2](#decision-2-who-pays)), with the MCP line ([decision 4](#decision-4-make-mcp-the-stand-out-moment)).
6.  Slide 8: the course platforms and the line ([decision 5](#decision-5-name-the-course-platforms)).
7.  Slide 10: the only slide that names Live2D and ElevenLabs. Make the Claude model match the code.
8.  Slide 11: a closing slide in place of the mentor questions, with QR codes for the live demo and the code, the Connect Your AI page, and "Data decides. AI explains."
9.  If package B ran, add one line on what the testers said.

### Package D: video

#82 and #84, Saturday 2 PM to 11 PM.

1.  The first 15 to 30 seconds show the persona, the moment and their finished roadmap. The problem comes next.
2.  The narration follows [decision 3](#decision-3-narrate-what-the-user-or-payer-gets). Add "AI check-up" to the banned phrases in the video's QA script.
3.  Shots: keep D1 to D7, let Kopi's voice play in D6, and replace D8 with the MCP clip ([decision 4](#decision-4-make-mcp-the-stand-out-moment)).
4.  Team members narrate in their own voices at 1.0× speed **(human)**. The whole video runs 5:30 to 6:30, and the live demo at least 3:00.
5.  Upload as public, link the video in the README, open every link signed out, and submit by Saturday 11 PM **(human)**.

### Package E: judge questions

#85. Drill these new questions:

- Why digital workers and not the most vulnerable workers?
- Who pays, and how much? Answer with the model, not invented prices.
- How is Kotak different from MasterClass, ReSkills or e-LATiH?
- Is the employer team view built? No: it is the next step.
- Does the April-to-May change prove that the trend layer drives matching?

## Key interfaces

- `docs/demo/deck/pitch-deck.html` and `docs/demo/deck/assets/`: the deck source and its images.
- `apps/web/src/views/RoadmapView.tsx` and `apps/web/src/views/roadmap/RoadmapTimeline.tsx`: the roadmap.
- `apps/web/src/demo/data.ts`: the sample profile with real courses.
- `packages/shared/src/data/role-corners.ts` (`FreeResourceSchema`) and `data/generated/role-corners.json`: the resource data.
- `apps/web/src/views/landing/LandingEvidence.tsx`: the Live2D credit.
- `docs/demo/video.md`: the video plan, the shot list and the quality checks.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deck slides 1 to 4 name one group, one moment and what the person walks away with, and no slide calls Kotak an "AI check-up" (proof: exported PDF).
- [ ] The deck has a "Who pays" slide, and every number on it has a source (proof: PDF page).
- [ ] Slide 8 names MasterClass, ReSkills and e-LATiH, with the positioning line (proof: PDF page).
- [ ] Slide 10 names the Claude model the code uses (proof: the PDF page matches `apps/api/src/ai/claude.ts`).
- [ ] Slide 11 is a closing slide with QR codes and the Connect Your AI page (proof: PDF page).
- [ ] The sample roadmap shows a cost on every step and one HRD Corp card that states rules, not courses (proof: screenshots at 1440 and 390 px).
- [ ] The Live2D credit is still on the landing page (proof: screenshot).
- [ ] The video opens on the persona and their roadmap, includes the MCP clip, and runs 5:30 to 6:30 (proof: QA script output).
- [ ] The captions don't contain "Live2D", "ElevenLabs" or "AI check-up" (proof: search of the caption file).

## How to test

- **Deck:** open `pitch-deck.html` in Chrome, step through every slide, export the PDF and the PPTX, and check each slide for overflow, as #215 did.
- **Roadmap:** run `bun run build && PORT=5180 bun run start`, open the sample profile's roadmap, and take screenshots at 1440 and 390 px, in light and dark.

## Must not change

- Verdict rules, fit maths and the 923-job engine.
- The signed PDFs in `submission/`.
- The Live2D credit on the landing page.
- The "Sample Data" and "self-reported" labels.

## Out of scope

- "What suits the company you want to join" (mentor point 3) maps to the paste-a-job-ad panel, #105, which stays with its own issue.
- Committing the transcript, or naming the mentor, anywhere in this public repository.

## Blocked by

None. The organiser's approval for this repository (#260) is also P0 and runs in parallel.

## Done means

A judge who has never met us can say, after the video, who Kotak is for, what that person walks away with, who pays, and why Kotak is more than another chatbot.

items.title: Renewal & promo banners — align 3.24 beta wording with Plugin banners requirements

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: Indicates an unexpected problem or unintended behavior

labels.name: priority: high
labels.description: Issues which should be resolved as quickly as possible

items.body:
## 🧠 Context

On 3.24 beta, the license banners on the WP Rocket dashboard use different wording than the [Plugin banners requirements](https://app.notion.com/p/wpmedia/Plugin-banners-2eeed22a22f080e4b9c9ecf9ed2b8a4f). A QA comparison found 11 differences across the five banners ([mismatch report](https://claude.ai/artifact/1FURSgRHXXT1buQESCJHrn)).

Reported on Slack: for Multi50 (also Plus and Single) customers whose account was created in 2020 or 2021, the renewal-soon banner shows the old grandfathered-discount wording instead of the required text. None of the expired banners shows the renewal price either.

## 🪲 Reproduce the problem

1. On 3.24 beta, use a Multi50, Plus or Single license created in 2020 or 2021 (grandfathered pricing).
2. Set the license to expire in less than 30 days, then open the WP Rocket dashboard.
3. Compare the banner text with the table below.
4. Repeat with an expired license (with and without Optimize CSS Delivery enabled, and at 0–15 days, 15–90 days and 90+ days since expiry).

## 💡 Expected behavior

Every banner shows exactly the wording from the requirements. The renewal-soon banner shows the renewal price for every license type (except type -1, which has no price line). The expired variants that need a price show it. Grandfathered customers see the same wording as everyone else.

| Banner | Element | Requirement | Actual in 3.24 beta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Promo | Title | It's [campaign]! | "{name} promotion is live!" with a "{N}% off" label |
| Promo | Message | Take advantage of [campaign] to speed up more websites: get a [Discount] off for upgrading your license to [license]! Hurry up, deal ends in: | Same, but the "Hurry up, deal ends in:" sentence is missing |
| Promo | CTA | Upgrade Now | Upgrade WP Rocket |
| Renewal soon | Title | Your license is about to expire! | Your WP Rocket license is about to expire. |
| Renewal soon | Message | You will soon lose the features that keep your site fast, plus access to updates and support. Renew now at [Renewal price amount] (excl. taxes) and keep your site optimized. | Line 1: You will soon lose access to product updates and support. Line 2: Renew before it is too late, you will pay {price}! (excl. taxes). Grandfathered users get a discount version of line 2 that the requirement no longer includes. Line 2 is hidden for license type -1. |
| Expired (standard) | Title | Your WP Rocket license has expired! | Your WP Rocket license is expired! |
| Expired (standard) | Message | Your site has stopped getting faster. You're missing out on the latest speed boosts, new features, and enhancements. Renew your license now at [Renewal Price amount] (excl. taxes). | Your website could be much faster if it could take advantage of our new features and enhancements. No price line |
| Expired (OCD active) | Title | Your license has expired. Keep your speed gains! | You will soon lose access to some features. |
| Expired (OCD active) | Message | Your CSS optimization will stop working on [expiration date + 15 days], and your pages will slow down, affecting your traffic and conversions. You'll also lose access to plugin updates and support. | You need an active license to continue optimizing your CSS delivery. The Remove Unused CSS and Load CSS asynchronously features are great options to address the PageSpeed Insights recommendations and improve your website performance. These features will be automatically disabled on {expiry + 15 days}. No mention of updates, support or traffic |
| Expired (OCD disabled) | Title | The Optimize CSS Delivery feature is now disabled | The Optimize CSS Delivery feature is disabled. |
| Expired (OCD disabled) | Message | You need an active license to keep optimizing your CSS delivery, which addresses a PageSpeed Insights recommendation and improves your page performance. Renew your license now at [Renewal Price amount] (excl. taxes). | You can no longer use the Remove Unused CSS or Load CSS asynchronously options. You need an active license to keep optimizing your CSS delivery, which addresses a PageSpeed Insights recommendation and improves your page performance. No price line |

The date in the OCD-active banner is correct (expiry plus 15 days).

## 🛠️ Implementation hints

> Note: These are findings from the drafting pass, not a finalized plan — treat them as a lead to verify, not a spec to follow blindly. The codebase may have moved on, or the read may be incomplete; confirm against the current code before implementing.

- The banner logic is in `inc/Engine/License/Renewal.php` and the templates are in `inc/Engine/License/views/` (`renewal-soon-banner.php`, `renewal-expired-banner.php`, `renewal-expired-banner-ocd.php`, `renewal-expired-banner-ocd-disabled.php`, `promo-banner.php`). Verify against the 3.24 beta branch; the strings above come from the beta build.
- The grandfathered wording comes from the `is_grandfather()` branch in `get_banner_data()`. It could be dropped, which would explain why 2020/2021 customers see different text.
- The expired templates already support an optional `message` paragraph, but `display_renewal_expired_banner()` always passes `null`. One option is to pass the formatted renewal price there.
- The price helper in `get_banner_data()` already formats the price with currency and "(excl. taxes)", so it could be reused.
- Strings are translatable, so the changes will affect the translation files.

## 📍 Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The promo banner title, message and CTA match the requirement, including "Hurry up, deal ends in:" before the countdown.
- [ ] The renewal-soon title and message match the requirement and show the renewal price with "(excl. taxes)".
- [ ] The renewal-soon banner shows the same wording for grandfathered (Multi50, Plus, Single, created 2020/2021) and non-grandfathered customers, with no grandfathered-discount line.
- [ ] The standard expired banner title and message match the requirement and show the renewal price.
- [ ] The OCD-active expired banner title and message match the requirement, with expiry + 15 days as the date.
- [ ] The OCD-disabled expired banner title and message match the requirement and show the renewal price.
- [ ] Existing tests are updated for the new strings and pass.

## ℹ️ Additional information

- Requirements: [Plugin banners (Notion)](https://app.notion.com/p/wpmedia/Plugin-banners-2eeed22a22f080e4b9c9ecf9ed2b8a4f)
- Mismatch report: [WP Rocket 3.24-beta: Banner Wording Mismatches](https://claude.ai/artifact/1FURSgRHXXT1buQESCJHrn)
- Requirement wording above was copied from the mismatch report, not re-checked against Notion.

#### ❓ Open questions

- Should the renewal-soon banner show the grandfathered discount anywhere, or drop it everywhere as the requirement implies?
- What should the renewal-soon banner show for license type -1, which currently has no price line?

#### 🥼 QA

Check each banner on a grandfathered license (Multi50, Plus, Single created in 2020/2021) and on a non-grandfathered license, for all five banner states.

#### ⏳ Effort estimation

**S** — Mostly string and template changes across five banners, plus passing the renewal price to the expired banners and updating tests.

#### 📦 Delivery estimation

Code only

#### 💥 Risks

**Low** — Text and template changes; the price display for expired users and the removed grandfathered line are the only logic touched.

---

items.body:
## Context

`publier-app` runs on every merge on `v2` and fails every time: the signing secrets are missing (#1441), so nothing is published. In one day that made 29 failed runs, each one an email to the chef. The chef will not pay for an Apple Developer account for now, and has no Windows certificate either.

He wants an intermediate path: on each new version, the Mac, Windows and Android apps show a banner with a direct link to download the new package. Fully automatic, signed self-update stays in #1150, for the day certificates exist.

## Acceptance criteria

- When the signing secrets are missing, a merge that changes the app still publishes a release `app-v<version>` with the three packages, unsigned: the Mac `.dmg`, the Windows installer and the Android `.apk`. The run is green and says in one line that the builds are unsigned.
- When the secrets are present, the signed path of #1441 is unchanged.
- A merge that does not change the app publishes nothing and sends no failure.
- When a newer `app-v` release exists, the app on Mac, Windows and Android shows a banner: "Version X available — Download", with a direct link to the package for its own platform (not to the releases page).
- On Mac and Windows, the banner says in one line how to open an unsigned app the first time: on Mac, right click then Open; on Windows, SmartScreen's "More info" then "Run anyway".
- The banner can be dismissed for this version, and comes back for the next one.
- An app already on the latest version shows no banner.

**2/3 servis.**

items.title: Free code signing via SignPath Foundation and Smart App Control validation (after v1)
items.body:
Part of #78

## Why
Deferred by owner answer O3 (#6): v1 ships unsigned. Smart App Control (SAC) in enforcement mode blocks an unsigned, zero-reputation exe outright, with no "Run anyway", so free signing is the first thing after v1. The owner will never pay for a certificate (O6): this issue covers SignPath Foundation only; the Microsoft Store MSIX channel is the second free path (#85). It has to be proven on a real SAC-enforcing machine, not assumed.

## Scope
- Apply to SignPath Foundation (owner action, after v1.0 with a few public releases) and, once accepted, implement it in the signing hook of the release pipeline (#73):
  - **SignPath**: upload the unsigned exes as a workflow artifact, submit a signing request through SignPath's GitHub Actions integration, wait for the manual approval (owner = approver), download the signed files. Artifact configuration with file metadata restrictions: product name `PeekBuddy`, product version equal to the release version (VERSIONINFO from winresource 0.1.34, #59).
- Every PE is signed: RSA (2048+), SHA-256 digest, RFC 3161 timestamp. Today that is one exe per architecture; the gate fails if an unexpected PE (DLL, helper exe) appears in an archive.
- arm64 exes are signed from an x64 job if the signing tool is x64-only.
- Order: build -> sign -> verify -> zip, SHA256SUMS, SBOM, attestations -> publish. Nothing touches a PE after signing (no UPX, no resource patching).
- Signing credentials live in a GitHub environment `release` with the owner as required reviewer; MFA on GitHub and SignPath for every team member.
- **CI gate** (release.yml, runs on every rc and release): for every PE in every archive, `signtool verify /pa /v` exits 0, the signature is timestamped, the digest is SHA-256, the key is RSA, and the signer subject equals the expected value pinned in the workflow.
- **SAC validation** of a release candidate (x64 in a VM on the owner's PC through a scripted owner run, #86; arm64 has no device (O4) and stays a documented gap):
  1. Clean Windows 11 25H2 VM; force SAC on via the documented `VerifiedAndReputablePolicyState=1` procedure.
  2. `citool.exe -lp` shows enforcement (VerifiedAndReputableDesktop, not the Evaluation policy).
  3. Additionally apply the `SmartAppControlAuditNoISG` policy so the test proves the signature path, not cloud reputation.
  4. Download from the GitHub release in a browser (Mark of the Web), unzip, run all roles: engine, tray, `--viewer`, export, autostart toggle, `--diagnostics`, `--perf-probe`.
  5. CodeIntegrity Operational log has no event 3077 (or 3033) for PeekBuddy; screenshots and `citool` output go to `docs/spikes/` or the release checklist.
- SmartScreen check on a non-SAC VM: capture the "Windows protected your PC" prompt for docs.
- Docs: `docs/code-signing-policy.md` linked from README under a "Code signing policy" heading (SignPath wording: "Free code signing provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation", team roles, privacy statement); extend `docs/how-to/verify-download.md` and `docs/explanation/smartscreen-and-smart-app-control.md` from #87 with signature checks (Get-AuthenticodeSignature/signtool) and remove the "Unsigned builds" wording.

## Out of scope
- Any paid certificate: Certum, Azure Artifact Signing, OV, EV (O6). MSIX/Store signing is #85.
- If SignPath rejects: record the reason here, keep the #87 docs as the user-facing answer, and re-apply after more release history.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] rc and release builds of both architectures are signed; the signing gate in release.yml passes and is proven to fail on an unsigned exe (negative test via `workflow_dispatch` input).
- [ ] SHA256SUMS and attestations describe the signed files (checked by re-hashing the downloaded assets).
- [ ] SAC validation done on a clean 25H2 VM in enforcement + NoISG audit with evidence attached; no 3077 events.
- [ ] Docs above exist and are linked from README; the SignPath policy text matches its terms.
- [ ] If SignPath is used: approval flow documented in `docs/how-to/release.md`.

## Performance & quality gates
- Size budget re-checked on the signed exe (signature adds a few KB; `budgets.toml` cap still applies).
- Engine "ready" (F7) measured once on the SAC VM signed vs. unsigned as an informational data point; not a gate (F11).
- Signing gate is deterministic and blocks publishing.

## Notes & gotchas
- SAC checks every PE the loader touches, not only downloaded files; one unsigned DLL blocks the app (logseq/og#55).
- ECC signatures are documented as unsupported by SAC; use RSA.
- A valid signature does not override an ISG malware/PUA verdict; keep behaviour free of PUA-like traits.
- A fresh VM may sit in SAC Evaluation (nothing blocked) for weeks: always confirm with `citool.exe -lp`. Forcing modes needs admin, BitLocker suspension and WinRE steps; use a disposable VM.
- KB5127648 (2026-10-13) can grey out the SAC toggle on PCs where it was Off (known issue, registry workaround).
- SignPath: publisher shown is "SignPath Foundation", every release needs manual approval, acceptance is discretionary and reputation-based (a new project was rejected 2026-10-07).

items.body:
Surfaced by Phase 8e Task 2, 2026-10-23, as a blast radius rather than as a defect.

## What happened

Adding two required methods to `ApiClient` (`exportCandidateData`, `deleteCandidateData` in `apps/web/src/lib/api.ts`) broke **22 test files**. Not because any of them exercise candidate erasure — none do — but because each file defines its own local `fakeClient()` fixture, and a required method added to the interface makes every hand-rolled stub incomplete at once.

Each had to be stubbed individually, matching that file's existing style, and every one re-run to confirm.

## Why it is worth fixing

The cost is paid by whoever next adds a method to `ApiClient`, and it scales with the number of test files rather than with the size of the change. It also creates pressure in the wrong direction: an implementer facing 22 incidental edits is tempted to make the method optional, or to avoid adding it to the interface at all, which weakens the type that was supposed to be the contract.

This phase has several more `ApiClient` additions coming — 8b's grading queue, 8c's exports, 8d's webhook panel — so the next few tasks will each pay it again.

## What it would take

One shared fixture helper exporting a complete default `ApiClient` stub, with each test overriding only the methods it actually asserts on. Then an added method is one edit, and a test that cares about it opts in.

**Deliberately not done inside 8e Task 2** — a 22-file refactor landing inside an `S-14` erasure task would have made that diff unreviewable, and the review of a destructive, Owner-only data-deletion path is not where anyone should be reading fixture churn. Filed instead, which is the right trade.

Not urgent. Worth doing before the remaining Phase 8 panels land rather than after.

items.body:
## Parent

#6 — the first playable milestone.

## What to build

**Orders** — the game's primary transaction, and the dependable floor under speculation's ceiling
(findings §2.1).

An order is a want a buyer states plainly **with the price they will pay**. Dependable both ways: it completes
only at **acceptable** or better, a near-miss is **declined rather than bought cheap**, and it stays open
until it is filled or its date passes. An accepted order is also the strongest form of plan declaration this
milestone has.

An order's price is stated, so no premium rides on one. Its desire can be in either register — a price on a
vague want is still an order — which is why this is blocked on vague wants existing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A buyer offers an order stating what is wanted, where, by when and for what price.
- [ ] Accepting one is a command; the accepted order appears on its own read model.
- [ ] Filling it pays the **stated price**, not a computed offer.
- [ ] It completes only at acceptable or better; a grudging match is **declined**, leaving the order open and
      the good in the hold.
- [ ] It stays open until filled or until its date passes, and a failed attempt costs nothing but time.
- [ ] An order whose date has passed closes, and the digest says so.
- [ ] Orders exist in both desire registers, and the CSV splits open orders **plain and vague** and reports
      how many are fillable from stock the tourist has seen.
- [ ] The page shows open orders with their dates and prices.
